# Multi-source SI network — Plan S3-E3: stage-3 P5 database groups, placement, seal key, readiness, re-selection and checkpoints, arbiter consensus Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

> **Status (2026-10-16): draft.** Tasks 71, 72, 73, 74, 75 are drafted and were verified by their drafters in scratch exports; no task has had its adversarial review yet, and the plan consistency pass (which also writes Appendices B and C in final form) and the cross-plan pass have not run. Do not execute this plan before those passes; `2026-10-15-multi-source-si-s3cf-status.md` lists what remains and how to finish it.

**Goal:** Give the arbiter FSM the stage-3 group layer, all of it inert until its switch. Apply places a `DatabaseGroup` per (owner, database) by integer weighted rendezvous hashing when a database gains its first physical incarnation, and the `placement` switch-on backfills every existing database (genesis-origin ones included) and seals the open block at a recorded cutover. Groups change only through the authority-signed `RebalanceGroup` (Raft tag 38). That command checks a generation, seals first with the C10 discipline and records Leaving members with their frozen E. Blocks seal on (owner, `GroupKey`), headers sealed after the cutover carry `group_key`, transition blocks carry one key's changes, and the leader's grouping window keys on the same pair. Three more commands complete the layer. Members declare readiness with an ed25519-signed `MemberReady` (tag 40) and then enter eligible rings. The leader replaces dead, ineligible or timed-out verifiers of an unlatched block with an authority-signed `ReselectVerifiers` (tag 39), timed by the committed L2 registry cursor so it fires on a quiet track too. Replicate members sign `MemberCheckpoint`s (tag 41) with their `replica_signer`, under a durable `checkpoint_seq` per (member, owner), which drive per-(member, group) classes with bounded lag accounting and the authority-signed `MarkMemberLagging` (tag 42). Every rule replays on restore and every signature is re-verified under its own epoch. With every switch off, each Apply, snapshot and chain hash is byte for byte what Plan S3-E2's branch produces.

**Architecture:** Every task is arbiter code on the shared P5 branch `urwt/claude/multi-source-s3e`, on top of Plan S3-E2's Tasks 64–70; no task cuts a release. Task 71 adds the group records:
- `fsm/stage3_groups.go`: `DatabaseGroup`, `GroupMember`, `LeavingMember`, the durable `GroupGenerations`, and the E set `copyFloorSetLocked` that Plan S3-E4's floor reads.
- `fsm/placement.go`: the exported pure placement function `PlaceGroup` and its frozen digest vectors.
- Placement on `AddTable`, the backfill on the `placement` switch-on, group removal at the last purge, and `purge_members` accumulation.
- `fsm/rebalance_group.go`: `RebalanceGroup` with its Leaving records; the per-group verifier floor.
- The registry view's `groups`, `ConsensusAdmin.RebalanceGroup`, and `arbiter-admin group rebalance`, `group preview` and `consensus groups`.

Task 72 adds the seal key:
- `fsm/group_key.go`: `GroupKey`, `GroupSeal` and `SealKey`.
- The open block and `BlockVerification` record the group seal; admission seals on (owner, key); `RebalanceGroup`, a params update that changes a key and the placement switch-on seal first.
- Headers carry `L3BlockTrack.group_key` after the recorded cutover; transition blocks are planned per (owner, key).
- `server/grouper.go` orders by `SealKey`; the node-local counter `arbiter_block_seal_reason`; the header and `GetBlockVerification` serve the new fields; the new frozen `fsm/l3_group_key_golden_test.go`.

Task 73 adds `MemberReady`, `VerifierGateway.SubmitMemberReady`, and the group half of Plan S3-E2's eligible ring and of the `VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE` admission count. Task 74 adds `ReselectVerifiers`:
- The latched-refusal amendment with the latch count, deletion of the replaced verifiers' evidence, structural restore checks and per-epoch proof re-verification.
- The WorkSet row and the orchestrator's signed proposal.

Task 75 adds `MemberCheckpoint`:
- The durable, published `checkpoint_seq`; classes and hysteresis over the bounded `OwnerAdvances` ring; and `MarkMemberLagging` with its leader-local timeout proposal.
- `ConsensusAdmin.MarkMemberLagging`, `VerifierGateway.SubmitMemberCheckpoint` and `arbiter-admin member lagging`.
- Restore re-verification of every checkpoint under its epoch's `replica_signer`.

Plan S3-E4 (`2026-10-15-multi-source-si-s3e4-p5-floor-release-activation.md`) then adds the floor, strict mode, the Leaving release evaluation, the narrowed drain gate and the integration harness, and releases the branch as `ARBITER_TAG_P5`. Plan S3-F turns the switches on.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.26; Bazel 9.1.0 + Bzlmod + gazelle (arbiter); hashicorp/raft + raft-boltdb; the arbiter-proto, housegate and arbiter-core releases `PROTO_TAG_P5`, `HG_TAG_P5` and `CORE_TAG_P5` that Plan S3-E2 Task 64 pins; Prometheus client_golang; Python 3 (`python3 -I`, standard library only) for the independent recomputation of golden digests.

**Spec:** the spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-stage3-database-groups-design.md` in housegate, branch `urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-plans-cf` (PR housegate#236 with every review fix; the branch is aligned with main, which holds Plans S3-A and S3-B as housegate#237, D34). It binds as clarified by Plan S3-A's K1–K10, Plan S3-B's K11–K22, Plan S3-E1's K58–K67, Plan S3-E2's K68–K72 and this plan's K73–K77 below. This plan implements, for the arbiter only:

## Global Constraints

- **Plans S3-A, S3-B, S3-E1 and S3-E2 apply.** Every Global Constraint and clarification of those plans applies, and through them those of Plans S1-A, S1-B, S2-A and S2-B: the strict decoder, request-only signatures, signed claims, tracks, quarantine, golden files, worktrees, commits and remote actions.
- **Cross-plan decisions (stage-3 conventions D25–D40).** Six touch this plan; the others bind plans this one does not change:
  - D25: only Plans S3-D and S3-E1 change the count literals of arbiter-proto's `conformance/stage3_reads_test.go`. This plan edits no arbiter-proto file.
  - D26: `PROTO_TAG_P5` is built on Plan S3-D's unconditional `PROTO_TAG_P4`, with `ConsensusAdmin.RebalanceGroup` at method 16 and `MarkMemberLagging` at 17 of 18 (contract §49).
  - D27: the registry view serves each current member's `GroupMember.host_indexer_id`. It is filled when the view is read, from the member's listed `verifiers` entry, whose host is fixed for the entry's life (K68), and is absent while the member is delisted (K73). It is never FSM state (contract §50). Plan S3-E4 reads it instead of a `hostOf` mapping.
  - D31: `GroupMember.lag_advances` is `memberLagLocked`, which saturates at `max_lag_publications + 1` (K76, contract §50, §52.3).
  - D33: a read view exposes a field only when a runbook or live task reads it. `ReadySignature`, `ReadyEpoch`, a group's ready verify members and `Reselection.ExpectedSet` therefore stay unserved. A later plan that needs one adds it to the view in its own task and records it (contract §49).
  - D34: the ledger names this plan reads are read on their plans' ledger copies. That copy is the plans-cf branch until the stage-3 plans PR merges, then main (contract §49).
- **Registry view versions.** Every Apply that changes a value the registry view serves bumps the registry version once. That includes the values derived when the view is read: a group's key, a member's `host_indexer_id` and its `lag_advances`. The rule is contract §50's, and it follows the existing quarantine precedent (`arbiter:fsm/table_registry.go:285-292`). `WatchTableRegistry` followers therefore never see two contents under one version.
- **Activation model (contract §49):**
  - Every new Apply branch checks its switch first and returns the fixed refusal of contract §50–§52 with state unchanged: tags 38 and 40 before `placement`, tag 39 before `reselection`, tags 41 and 42 before `checkpoints`.
  - The leader proposes none of tags 38–42 before its switch.
  - Every new state field is `omitempty`: before `placement` no group exists, no header carries `group_key` and no open block or `BlockVerification` carries a group seal, so each Apply, snapshot and chain hash is byte-identical to Plan S3-E2's branch.
  - Nothing here changes the v21 framing, writes v21 earlier, or changes a frozen constant.
- **The `stage3_v1` release rule (K65):** this plan cuts no arbiter release, tag or image. Its commits stay on `urwt/claude/multi-source-s3e` until Plan S3-E4 Task 78 releases the branch as `ARBITER_TAG_P5`.
- **Determinism:**
  - Groups, keys, rings, re-selections and classes derive only from committed state and logged bytes.
  - The key reads committed group records and the `verifiers` listing, never node status. Eviction therefore never changes a chain hash or forces a seal (K73).
  - Lists are sorted where contract §50–§52 says so, and no map iteration order reaches state or a digest.
  - Placement and group-key digests use the existing `replay.CanonicalDigest` profile under the two new domains of contract §50–§51.
- **Ordering:** Tasks 71 → 72 → 73 → 74 → 75, each committed before the next starts. Tasks may be drafted in parallel, as "Task order and dependencies" says.
- **Irreversible steps:** none. No live, remote or consensus action is part of this plan. The one-way switches it implements are turned on by Plan S3-F, each as its own confirmed update.
- **production rule:** this plan changes no production file. The monitoring rules for the metrics of contract §51–§52 belong to Plan S3-E4 Task 80, and the runbook steps that use `arbiter-admin group rebalance`, `group preview`, `consensus groups` and `member lagging` belong to Plan S3-F Task 84.
- **Runbook conventions:** this plan writes no runbook and has no live block. Its CLI commands follow the existing `arbiter-admin` conventions of contract §50 and §52 (JSON on stdout, unknown commit outcomes named), so Plan S3-F's runbook blocks can call them under the S3-B runbook conventions.
- **Passwords and keys:**
  - `arbiter-admin` reads the authority key only from `ARBITER_AUTHORITY_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX` and never prints or logs it. Tests generate throwaway secp256k1 and ed25519 keys in code.
  - No key, password or token appears in a commit, a fixture, a log line or chat. The golden vectors hash public fixture values only.
- **Never edit existing golden or vector files:** everything Plans S2-A and S3-A list, `fsm/testdata/pre_tracks_golden.json`, the constants of `fsm/l3_track_golden_test.go` (and those of `l3_commitment_golden_test.go` and `l3_transition_golden_test.go`), and arbiter-proto's `conformance/stage3_reads_test.go`. Under D25 only that last file's count literals change, and only in Plans S3-D and S3-E1; every existing entry stays byte-identical. They must all pass as their owners left them, and so must Plan S3-E2's frozen v21 container vectors. New frozen fixtures of this plan:
  - `fsm/placement_golden_test.go` (placement digest, draws, scores, order and members);
  - `fsm/l3_group_key_golden_test.go` (`GroupKey` digests and the statement and transition header preimages with `group_key`).

  Their values are fixed in contract §50–§51 and recomputed independently by `python3 -I` in the task that writes them.
- **Repository commands, worktrees, commits:** contract §49. Remote actions (a push of the shared branch) require explicit user confirmation in chat. Commands handed to the user are fish.
- **Hunks are anchored on origin/main.** Every arbiter file this plan edits is also edited by Plan S3-A Tasks 7–11, Plan S3-D Task 51, Plan S3-E2 Tasks 64–70 or an earlier task of this plan. When a hunk overlaps such an edit, apply the later intent on top of the earlier change. The contract and the named tests are binding; line anchors are guidance.
- **References.** `contract §N` points to:
  - Appendix A of Plan S3-A for §0–§6;
  - Appendix A of Plan S3-B for §7–§15;
  - Appendix A of Plans S3-E1 and S3-E2 for §38–§48;
  - this plan's Appendix A for §49–§52.

  A task group's "Facts" point to Appendix B. Appendix C holds no ledger names (contract §49) and records nothing.

## Plan clarifications (binding)

The spec and Plans S3-E1 and S3-E2 leave these details open. Each is resolved here and binds Plans S3-E3, S3-E4 and S3-F.

- **K73 — Membership versus delisting, eviction and `group_size` (spec §6.4 versus §7.1, §7.3, §9.3).**
  - *Gap:* §6.4 changes a placed group "only through an authority-signed `RebalanceGroup`". But §7.1 says a `ConsensusParamsUpdate` that "flips an entry's `verify` flag or delists it" changes the key, and §9.3 says "eviction or delisting removes a member from E in the same Apply".
  - *Resolution:*
    - `DatabaseGroup.Members` changes only through placement, the switch-on backfill, `RebalanceGroup` and group removal.
    - Delisting a member (which also evicts it, `arbiter:fsm/signed_claims.go:277-287`) or flipping its `verify` flag leaves its `members` entry in place. In the same Apply it removes the member from every eligible ring and from E (both filter by listing and node status when they are evaluated) and from every key (the key filters by listing).
    - An `EvictNode` removes it from rings and E but not from any key, because the key never reads node status.
    - The registry view serves a current member's `host_indexer_id` from its listed entry. A delisted member is therefore served without one (D27), and the update that delists it bumps the registry version (contract §50).
    - Raising `group_size` re-places no group; only placements made afterwards use the new size.
    - The per-group verifier floor counts a group's listed, non-evicted members with `verify`, plus the listed, non-evicted pool entries while the group's `network_fill` is on.
  - *Why:* §6.2 makes `members` "the chosen list itself", so auditors compare against it; recomputing it from the listing would break that. A key that read node status would change on a command that never seals (`EvictNode`), and voters would then disagree about an open block's key. Counting only verify members keeps the floor about verifiers, as the global floor of three verifiers is.
- **K74 — The Leaving record (spec §6.4 as amended).**
  - *Gap:* the amended non-strict release counts "members of E other than the Leaving member, in at least min(k − 1, |E|) distinct failure domains (E and |E| … both evaluated as they were when the `RebalanceGroup` applied)", which needs state the spec does not name.
  - *Resolution:*
    - A member that `RebalanceGroup` removes moves from `Members` to `DatabaseGroup.Leaving` as a `LeavingMember` with class `leaving`. The record keeps its `GroupMember` record, `RemovedGeneration` (the generation that command set), `Entry` (O's latest published entry at that Apply), `FrozenE` (the sorted node ids of E at that Apply, the Leaving member excluded) and `FrozenEDomains` (|E| at that Apply). The node joins `PastMembers` in the same Apply.
    - Plan S3-E4 Task 76 sets `Released` the first time the release condition holds and never clears it. A record leaves `Leaving` only when the same node is added to the group again, which replaces it with a fresh `GroupMember` at the new generation.
    - Leaving members enter no eligible ring and no key, may not checkpoint, and keep verifying only where an unfinished block's stored verify set already names them.
  - *Why:* the non-strict rule freezes E at the `RebalanceGroup`, so the frozen set must be stored. It is bounded by the group's candidate count, and recording it once makes the later release a pure function of committed state.
- **K75 — Re-selection records (spec §7.4).**
  - *Gap:* §7.4 says replaced verifiers' evidence "is ignored" but does not say whether it stays in state. It does not name the clock fields or the record restore checks.
  - *Resolution:*
    - `ReselectVerifiers` deletes the replaced verifiers' `Attestations`, `ByteScans` and `Verdict.Replicas` entries in the same Apply, then re-evaluates the block.
    - Each applied command appends a `Reselection{ExpectedSet, Replaced, Replacements, RingPosition, CursorBlock, AuthorityJWS, AuthorityEpoch}`. `ExpectedSet` is stored for the proof and is not served (D33).
    - The timeout compares the committed registry cursor's `BlockNumber` with the larger of `MarkedCursorBlock` (Plan S3-E2 §48) and the last `Reselection.CursorBlock`, plus `evidence_timeout_l2_blocks`.
    - The latch records `ThreeWayVerdict.ReselectionsAtLatch`.
    - Only the leader proposes the command: there is no operator RPC, as the spec has none.
  - *Why:* deleting the evidence makes "evidence keys ⊆ `VerifierSet`" a restore invariant, and late evidence from a replaced verifier is already refused by the set check at `arbiter:fsm/apply.go:598-600` and `:627-629`. `ExpectedSet` is the signed value, so restore can re-verify the proof. The two cursor fields make the quiet-track timeout a pure function of committed state.
- **K76 — Bounded lag state and checkpoint ordering (spec §9.1, §9.2).**
  - *Gap 1:* §9.1 asks that a checkpoint's manifest be "on the watermark chain … and not earlier on the chain than the member's previous checkpoint". Manifests carry no publication ordinal, and a parent walk is unbounded.
  - *Gap 2:* §9.2 counts lag "in published advances of O". The scoping proposal's "parent walk of at most `max_lag_publications + 1` steps" bounds manifests visited, not O's advances. A quiet owner's advances can sit behind any number of other owners' publications, so the walk would undercount.
  - *Resolution:*
    - A manifest is on the watermark chain iff it is in `State.Manifests`, because every publication's parent is the current watermark (`arbiter:fsm/manifest_validation.go:51`, `:111`).
    - Restore checks the same binding again: every stored checkpoint, a Leaving record's included, names a manifest of `State.Manifests` whose `track_frontiers` entry for its owner is its entry, and every recent advance is an entry such a manifest carries for its owner (contract §52.3). No Apply removes a manifest (both writes to `State.Manifests` add one: `arbiter:fsm/apply.go:945`, `arbiter:fsm/apply_snapshot_query_abort.go:248`), and restore keeps every track-aware manifest on the watermark's chain (`validateRestoredTrackChain`, `arbiter:fsm/genesis_validation.go`), so a bound entry is never past the published one.
    - "Not earlier" is decided on the entry: the new entry must not precede the member's previous checkpoint entry for O in the order (`safe_block_seq`, `applied_promotion_seq`). Every consumer of a checkpoint (classes, E, the floor) reads only its entry, and entries never decrease along the chain.
    - Lag is kept per owner in `Stage3State.OwnerAdvances`: the last `max_lag_publications + 1` distinct entries O's published entry advanced to while O was not quarantined, appended by `applyPublishSafeSnapshot` from the `checkpoints` switch on, oldest dropped.
    - A member's lag in a group is the number of those entries after its checkpoint entry, so it saturates at `max_lag_publications + 1`.
    - The registry view serves that saturating count as `GroupMember.lag_advances` (0 without a checkpoint, D31). A publication that changes it bumps the registry version (contract §52.3).
  - *Why:* this keeps O(owners × `max_lag_publications`) state with no history and no walk (spec §2: state already grows quadratically). It counts exactly what §9.2 names, honours "a quarantined owner accrues no lag", and restore can check it.
- **K77 — `MarkMemberLagging` (spec §9.2, §16 operator playbook).**
  - *Gap:* §9.2 has the orchestrator propose it "after a timeout" and the playbook says "wait for or issue `MarkMemberLagging`", but neither says who may issue it, which timeout applies or what Apply re-checks.
  - *Resolution:* both the leader and the operator may issue it.
    - **Operator:** `ConsensusAdmin.MarkMemberLagging` exists, authority-signed like `QuarantineIndexer`, together with `arbiter-admin member lagging`.
    - **Leader:** the orchestrator proposes it when a member's checkpoint entry has stayed behind O's published entry for `dispatch.member_lagging_timeout` (default `30m`, `0` disables), measured leader-locally from the first WorkSet that shows that checkpoint entry behind. It uses the published entry as `observed_entry`.
    - **What Apply re-checks:** the `checkpoints` switch; the group and the member's current membership; class `caught_up` or `behind`; O not quarantined; `observed_entry` strictly after the member's checkpoint entry and at or before O's published entry.
  - *Why:* the playbook needs the command when the leader's timer has not fired (a leader change restarts it). The re-check keeps a stale or replayed command from marking a member that has since caught up.

## Review Focus

1. **A group key that two voters compute differently, or a `group_key` on the wrong block.** The key enters the chain hash, which is anchored on L2, so any disagreement forks the network.
   - *Expected:*
     - `GroupKey` hashes only the sorted ready verify members (committed group records filtered by the `verifiers` listing) and the group's fill flag, never node status.
     - Blocks at or below the recorded placement cutover, the cutover block itself included, carry no `group_key`, and every later block, transition blocks included, carries it.
     - A header with an empty key hashes exactly as today.
     - Restore refuses a key before the cutover, a missing key after it, and a key that differs from its recorded members and fill.
   - *Tests:*
     - Task 72: `TestL3GroupKeyHeaderPreimagesAreFrozen`, `TestGroupKeyGoldenVectorsAreFrozen`, `TestGroupKeyIgnoresEvictionAndNodeStatus`, `TestBlocksSealedAfterTheCutoverCarryGroupKeyAndEarlierOnesDoNot`, `TestRestoreRefusesAGroupKeyBeforeTheCutoverOrMissingAfterIt`.
     - The existing `TestL3TrackHeaderPreimagesAreFrozen` and `TestL3BlockHeaderMirrorsProto`, unchanged.
2. **A key-changing command while the open block holds a statement of the group.** The commands are the `placement` switch-on, `RebalanceGroup`, `MemberReady`, and a params update that flips `verify` or delists a member.
   - *Expected:*
     - The open block is sealed first under its old key with the C10 discipline: the seal is prepared before any mutation, and the command is refused with state unchanged when it cannot be.
     - Afterwards the open block's key always equals the current key of each statement's group.
     - Databases whose keys are equal keep sharing blocks, and before placement the owner-switch seal is today's.
   - *Tests:*
     - Task 71: `TestRebalanceGroupSealsAnOpenBlockHoldingTheDatabaseFirst`, `TestRebalanceGroupRefusesWithStateUnchangedWhenTheSealCannotBePrepared`.
     - Task 72: `TestPlacementSwitchOnSealsTheOpenBlockAndRecordsTheCutover`, `TestParamsUpdateFlippingVerifySealsFirst`, `TestParamsUpdateDelistingAMemberSealsFirst`, `TestKeyChangeSealRefusesWithStateUnchangedWhenItCannotBePrepared`, `TestDatabasesWithEqualKeysShareABlock`, `TestOwnerSwitchSealIsUnchangedBeforePlacement`, `TestRestoreRefusesAnOpenBlockKeyThatDiffersFromItsGroups`.
     - Task 73: `TestMemberReadyChangesTheKeyAndSealsAnOpenBlockOfTheGroupFirst`.
3. **Placement that an auditor cannot re-derive.** The risky inputs are weights, failure-domain or host collisions, the salt of a genesis-origin or re-placed database, the backfill order, and generations after removal.
   - *Expected:*
     - The placement and its order are a pure function of the committed entries, the salt and the network id, frozen by digest vectors.
     - A candidate whose host or domain is already used, by the owner included, is skipped, and fill is forced on below three verify members.
     - The backfill places every database with a physical incarnation in (owner, database) order, or refuses the switch-on with state unchanged when a group would fall below the per-group floor.
     - A removed group's generation survives, so an old `RebalanceGroup` or `MemberReady` cannot be replayed against its re-placement.
     - `arbiter-admin group preview` prints exactly what Apply will place.
     - The registry view serves each current member's `host_indexer_id` from its listed entry (indexer 0 included), and serves none for a delisted member (D27). Any update that changes a member's entry bumps the registry version.
   - *Tests:*
     - Task 71: `TestPlacementGoldenVectorsAreFrozen`, `TestPlacementScoreIsTheMaxOverWeightDraws`, `TestPlacementSkipsUsedHostsAndFailureDomains`, `TestPlacementForcesFillBelowThreeVerifyMembers`, `TestPlacementSwitchOnBackfillsEveryDatabaseInOwnerDatabaseOrder`, `TestPlacementSwitchOnRefusesAGroupBelowTheFloorWithStateUnchanged`, `TestPlacementSaltOfAGenesisOriginDatabaseIsTheGenesisSnapshotID`, `TestGroupGenerationSurvivesRemovalAndReplacement`, `TestPlacementIsReDerivableFromTheRegistryView`, `TestGroupPreviewMatchesTheFSMPlacement`, `TestDeterminism_PlacementAndRebalance`, `TestRegistryViewServesMemberHostsFromTheListing`, `TestParamsUpdateChangingAMembersEntryBumpsTheRegistryVersion`.
4. **A re-selection racing the latch, an eviction or a quiet track.**
   - *Expected:*
     - A verifier is replaced only when it lacks complete evidence and is evicted, no longer eligible or timed out on the committed registry cursor; one with complete evidence is replaced only when evicted.
     - Replacements follow the stored ring after the stored position, and at most ring size − 3 re-selections are allowed.
     - Replaced verifiers' evidence is deleted, and their late evidence is refused.
     - After the latch the command is refused, the latch records the re-selection count, and the verdict survives the eviction of a passing verifier and a snapshot/restore.
     - On a track with no traffic the timeout still fires, because the cursor advances every `cursor_advance_interval`.
   - *Tests:*
     - Task 74: `TestReselectVerifiersReplacesOnlyIncompleteEvictedIneligibleOrTimedOut`, `TestAVerifierWithCompleteEvidenceIsReplacedOnlyIfEvicted`, `TestReplacementsFollowTheStoredRingAfterTheRingPosition`, `TestReplacedVerifiersEvidenceIsDeletedAndLateEvidenceRefused`, `TestReselectionIsLimitedToRingSizeMinusThree`, `TestReselectVerifiersOnAQuietTrackFiresOnTheRegistryCursor`, `TestReselectionIsRefusedAfterTheLatchAndTheVerdictSurvivesEvictionAndRestore`, `TestRestoreReverifiesReselectionProofsUnderTheirEpoch`.
5. **Checkpoint replay, a member that lost its state, and class flapping.**
   - *Expected:*
     - A replayed or lower `checkpoint_seq` is refused, at the same entry or any other.
     - A same-entry checkpoint replaces only the groups it lists and may shrink or grow their excluded sets.
     - The stored seq survives group removal, leaving and re-registration, restarts only when the `replica_signer` rotates, and is published, so a member that lost its state resumes above it.
     - Lag counts published advances of a non-quarantined owner from bounded per-owner state. The served `lag_advances` saturates at `max_lag_publications + 1` (D31), and every publication that can change it bumps the registry version.
     - A Lagging member returns to Behind only once it is past its observed entry with lag below `lag_low`.
     - `MarkMemberLagging` re-checks committed state.
     - Every stored checkpoint is re-verified under its own epoch's `replica_signer` on restore.
     - Restore binds every stored checkpoint, a Leaving record's included, to a published manifest whose `track_frontiers` entry for its owner is its entry, as Apply's refusals 12 and 13 do, so a member-signed checkpoint naming an unpublished manifest or a future entry cannot satisfy the copy floor or a Leaving release; every recent advance must be an entry a published manifest carries for its owner.
   - *Tests:*
     - Task 75: `TestAReplayedOrLowerCheckpointSeqIsRefused`, `TestASameEntryCheckpointReplacesOnlyItsListedGroups`, `TestASameEntryCheckpointMayShrinkOrGrowExcluded`, `TestCheckpointSeqIsDurableAcrossGroupRemovalLeavingAndReregistration`, `TestCheckpointSeqRestartsWhenTheReplicaSignerRotates`, `TestAMemberThatLostItsStateResumesAboveThePublishedSeq`, `TestLagIsCountedInPublishedAdvancesOfTheOwner`, `TestAQuarantinedOwnerAccruesNoLag`, `TestLaggingReturnsToBehindOnlyPastTheObservedEntryBelowLagLow`, `TestOwnerAdvancesStayBoundedByMaxLagPublications`, `TestRegistryViewLagAdvancesSaturatesAtMaxLagPublicationsPlusOne`, `TestPublicationBumpsTheRegistryVersionWhenAMemberHoldsACheckpoint`, `TestMarkMemberLaggingRefusals`, `TestRestoreReverifiesCheckpointSignaturesUnderEachEpochsReplicaSigner`, `TestRestoreRefusesAClassInconsistentWithItsCheckpoint`, `TestRestoreRefusesACheckpointOffItsPublishedManifest`.

## Follow-ups (not in this plan)

- **Group auditor:** the table-registry auditor (`arbiter:tableregistry/auditor.go`) could re-derive every placement with `fsm.PlaceGroup` and alert on a mismatch. That is cheap, but not required by the spec.
- **Operator re-selection:** `ReselectVerifiers` has no operator RPC (K75); if the leader's orchestrator is stuck, an operator's only lever is `EvictNode`.
- **Metric cardinality:** group metrics are labelled by owner only, so the label set stays bounded as tenants create databases. Per-database state is read from `arbiter-admin consensus groups`; a per-database gauge would need its own cardinality decision.
- **Placement preview:** `group preview` refuses while a listed host-bound entry is unregistered; a preview that models unregistered entries the way Apply does would need the leader's full node list, which no RPC serves (S3-E1 K64).
- **`max_lag_publications` changes:** a lowered value trims each owner's `OwnerAdvances` at once, so lag never exceeds the new bound. A raised one only takes effect as new advances accrue. Plan S3-F's runbook should state that.
- **The rest of P5 and P6:** the floor, strict mode, the Leaving release, the k raise, the narrowed drain gate, the integration harness and the release are Plan S3-E4. The switch-on of placement, re-selection and checkpoints is Plan S3-F. Mutation pre-state (§8.9), v22 and P8 have no task.

## Task 71: arbiter — database groups, placement and RebalanceGroup (S3-E3)

Spec §6.2–§6.4 give every (owner, database) with a physical incarnation exactly one `DatabaseGroup` from the `placement` switch (§10.4 step 5) on: chosen by integer weighted rendezvous hashing over the listed member entries of other SI indexers, with no two members on one host or in one failure domain and none on the owner's host or in its domain, re-derivable by any auditor from committed state, and changed afterwards only by an authority-signed `RebalanceGroup` (Raft tag 38) bound to the group's durable generation. Today nothing records a group: `applyAddTable` (`fsm/apply_table_registry.go:220-275`) appends incarnations, `completePurgesLocked` (`:496-521`) purges them, and Plan S3-E2 left `TableIncarnation.PurgeMembers`, the `placement` switch bit and the `stage3MembershipRefusalLocked` and `onStage3SwitchOnLocked` seams empty. This task adds the whole record layer of contract §50, all of it inert until the switch: the group records with their durable generations and Leaving records (K74); the exported pure `PlaceGroup` with its frozen digest vectors; placement at `AddTable`, the switch-on backfill (genesis-origin databases included) and group removal at the last purge; `purge_members` accumulation; `RebalanceGroup` with its 18 refusals, the C10 seal-first hook, Leaving records with frozen E and the `completePurgesLocked` rerun; the per-group verifier floor (K73); E (`copyFloorSetLocked`); the registry view's `groups` with each member's served `host_indexer_id` (D27) and the registry-version rule for served values; `ConsensusAdmin.RebalanceGroup`; `arbiter-admin consensus groups`, `group preview` and `group rebalance`; the group gauges; and the restore rules. With the switch off every Apply, snapshot and chain hash is byte for byte Plan S3-E2's.

Notes (each recorded in Appendix B):
- **Switch-off identity.** Every new state field is `omitempty`, and every new Apply branch needs the `placement` switch or an existing group: `RebalanceGroup` refuses first with contract §49's text, `applyAddTable` places nothing, the backfill plan is nil, `memberEntriesChangedLocked` needs a group, and `completePurgesLocked` drops or prunes nothing without one. `completePurgesReportLocked` reports exactly the old `purgedCount` change while no group exists, so `applyEvictNode` and `evictNodesLocked` bump the registry exactly as before. The switch-off history is therefore byte-identical to Plan S3-E2's branch (Plan S3-E4 Task 78's `TestPreActivationHistoryIsByteIdenticalAcrossStage3` pins it), and the existing goldens run unchanged.
- **Membership (K73).** `Members` changes only through placement, the backfill, `RebalanceGroup` and group removal. Delisting a member or flipping its `verify` keeps its record (`TestDelistingAMemberKeepsItsMembersEntry`); E and the per-group floor filter by the listing and node status when they are evaluated; `EvictNode` never runs the floor (`TestPerGroupVerifierFloorNeverRefusesEvictNode`); raising `group_size` re-places nothing.
- **Eviction under the next parameters.** The floor and the candidates of a consensus update are evaluated under `next` through `evictedUnderLocked`: a node is evicted if its record is `NodeEvicted` or if it is a registered verifier that `next` does not list under its registered key, the node rule 6 evicts in the same Apply (`signedClaimsMembershipLocked`, `fsm/signed_claims.go:219`). Under the committed parameters the second case never holds, so it is contract §50's "not `NodeEvicted`" there; a listed entry that never registered counts as non-evicted, as the contract says.
- **The backfill plan crosses into the turn-on hook.** Contract §50 computes the backfill "after the S3-E2 gates and before any mutation" and installs it "after `f.st.Params = next` and after §51's cutover seal", and Plan S3-E2 §44 puts the turn-on work in `onStage3SwitchOnLocked`. The plan therefore travels in the node-local FSM field `placementBackfill`, set right before `f.st.Params = next`, consumed and cleared by the `placement` case of the hook in the same Apply, and never snapshotted (it is nil between Applies). Task 72 commits its cutover seal in that case before the install.
- **One registry bump per Apply.** A placing `AddTable` ends with `groupsChangedLocked` instead of its usual `registryChangedLocked` (one bump either way). The switch-on is already bumped once by Plan S3-E2 Task 65's rule for a changed `stage3`, and installing the plan completes no purge and drops no group, so the install calls neither `groupsChangedLocked` nor `registryChangedLocked` (`TestPlacementSwitchOnBackfillsEveryDatabaseInOwnerDatabaseOrder` pins one bump); Plan S3-E4 Task 76's release evaluation has no Leaving record to look at there. `applyEvictNode` and the rule-6 evictions report through `completePurgesReportLocked`, which counts groups and past members as well as Purged incarnations, so an eviction that only prunes a past member or drops a group still reaches registry followers (`TestPastMembersLeaveOnlyByReportingOrEviction`).
- **Refusal order of `RebalanceGroup` (contract issue, recorded in Appendix B).** Contract §50 lists refusal 16 (`the result has %d verifiers, below the per-group floor of 3`) before 17 (`network_fill off needs at least 3 listed verify members, the result has %d`). With fill off the per-group floor counts exactly the listed, non-evicted verify members, which is at most what refusal 17 counts, so in that order refusal 17 could never fire and `TestRebalanceGroupRefusals` could not cover all 18. `rebalanceMembershipRefusalLocked` checks 17 first, then 16; both texts are verbatim, and every other refusal keeps the contract's order. The consistency pass should swap the two lines in contract §50.
- **`GroupView.Key` and `GroupMemberView.LagAdvances`.** Contract §50 gives the view types verbatim and maps `GroupView.Key` to `group_key` and `LagAdvances` to `lag_advances`, so this task declares both fields and maps them; they stay empty until Task 72 fills `Key` and Task 75 fills `LagAdvances` (`TestTableRegistryToPBCarriesGroups` pins the mapping). `GroupMember`'s Task 73 and Task 75 fields (`ReadyGeneration`, `ReadySignature`, `ReadyEpoch`, `Checkpoint *MemberCheckpointRecord`, `ObservedEntry`) are added by those tasks, because `MemberCheckpointRecord` is §52's type; Task 75 must extend `cloneDatabaseGroup` to deep-copy its two pointers.
- **`purge_members` restore rule (contract issue, recorded in Appendix B).** Plan S3-E2 §44 says Task 71 "adds the restore rule that [purge_members] is a subset of the group's members and past members", and Task 69 says Task 71 replaces its `purge_members before the placement switch` rule with it. Contract §50, which binds this task, lists the group restore rules without that subset rule, and the subset rule would refuse honest state: a past member leaves `past_members` once it has reported every incarnation that lists it or is evicted (§6.2), while those incarnations keep listing it, and a removed group's incarnations keep their `purge_members` with no group left. Task 71 therefore keeps both of Task 69's rules (the before-placement rule stays true, because the switch is one-way and only placement writes the field) and adds §50's rule that every current member is in `purge_members` of every physical incarnation of its database.
- **`stage3FieldsPresent` needs no new arm.** `Stage3State.Groups` and `GroupGenerations` live inside `doc.Stage3`, which Plan S3-E2 Task 66's `stage3FieldsPresent` already refuses in a pre-v21 container, and `purge_members` is Task 69's arm.
- **The pending proto map.** `TestTableRegistryMirrorsProto` walks only `TableIncarnation` and the cursor, so Plan S3-E2 Task 64 adds `TableRegistrySnapshot.groups` to `stage3PendingProtoFields` only if some other test failed on it; Step 25 deletes the entry when it exists and otherwise changes nothing.
- **Group preview is exact only with every member registered.** `GetNodeFeatures` lists the leader's non-evicted registrations, so a listed host-bound entry missing from it is either unregistered (which Apply counts as non-evicted) or evicted (which Apply skips); the preview refuses rather than guess (S3-E3 follow-up "Placement preview"). It reads quarantine from `GetTrackState` and the genesis snapshot id from `GetConsensusParams`, and calls the same `PlacementTargetsFrom`, `PlacementSaltFrom`, `PlacementCandidatesFrom` and `PlaceGroup` as Apply. `cmd/arbiter-admin` gains the `//fsm` dependency for them.
- **Metric label.** The group gauges label the SI indexer `owner` (contract §50), while the track gauges call it `indexer_id`; the `Metrics` doc comment now names both. Neither label set grows with tenants' databases.
- **Contract §49's base check (contract issue, recorded in Appendix B).** §49 stops Task 71 unless `git log --grep='(S3-E2 Task 70)'` prints a commit, but Plan S3-E2 §48 fixes its subjects as `feat(stage3): <what> (Task N)`, so that grep can never match. Step 1 greps Plan S3-E2's own subject form instead.

The anchors above are `526a721`'s; the shared branch starts at or after `ARBITER_TAG_P4`, which carries it.

```go
// Frozen placement vectors (plan S3-E3 contract §50). The values were
// recomputed outside Go (sha256 over "housegate-replay-mvp-v0:" + domain +

// here moves every group an auditor re-derives.
const (
	goldenPlacementPreimageJSON = `{"network_id":"net-1","owner":0,"database":"dex","salt":"0xabababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababab","node_id":"member-a","i":0}`
	goldenPlacementDrawA0       = "0xd28d6f586d9b5f674edc65298b947dd6384d93b55c89ab24fc354a6f4f285be8"
	goldenPlacementDrawB0       = "0x36ec8d28e07f7f36919adeae6e79e11d38ab5256cf804b3bb498ff4f0dd73ee3"
	goldenPlacementDrawB1       = "0xd93cfbba7dab2ad5847cc805baf27b9476bcbf45c4f09883241b49824ee5c06d"
	goldenPlacementDrawE0       = "0x23c6e7d5abc004a06621a187869ecd1b3b03e085b5476d8daa04419391e813cd"
	goldenPlacementDrawE1       = "0x64e502320ba93d7ea866ab7b870d814c3d10cec0ab0db6323f01b22684d0284f"
	goldenPlacementDrawE2       = "0x2c589bd8785d2f190d524337b058be8a8a1f2de279171538a6cc27c054690fc2"
	goldenPlacementScoreC       = "0x34f609e148ba75f98f3e836425e0984799d399a2e2e3710fe8530d12ab8f27ea"
	goldenPlacementScoreD       = "0x68c96aedfbd885ef76d7c0e16ed0dfd068195f1744d951722f0b4e987fce01a8"
)

var (
	goldenPlacementOrder   = []string{"member-b", "member-a", "member-d", "member-e", "member-c"} // d skipped "host", e skipped "failure_domain"
	goldenPlacementMembers = []string{"member-a", "member-b", "member-c"}                         // NetworkFill true
)

// goldenPlacementInput is the frozen fixture: owner 0 in domain node:o, five
// candidates, member-d sharing member-b's host and member-e sharing its
// failure domain.
func goldenPlacementInput() PlacementInput {
	return PlacementInput{NetworkID: "net-1", Owner: 0, OwnerFailureDomain: "node:o", Database: "dex",
		Salt: "0xabababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababab", GroupSize: 3, NetworkFillDefault: true,
		Candidates: []PlacementCandidate{
			{NodeID: "member-a", HostIndexerID: 1, FailureDomain: "node:a", Weight: 1, Verify: true},
			{NodeID: "member-b", HostIndexerID: 2, FailureDomain: "node:b", Weight: 2, Verify: true},
			{NodeID: "member-c", HostIndexerID: 3, FailureDomain: "node:c", Weight: 1, Verify: true},
			{NodeID: "member-d", HostIndexerID: 2, FailureDomain: "node:d", Weight: 1, Verify: true},
			{NodeID: "member-e", HostIndexerID: 4, FailureDomain: "node:b", Weight: 3, Verify: false},
		}}
}

func TestPlacementGoldenVectorsAreFrozen(t *testing.T) {
	in := goldenPlacementInput()
	pre, err := json.Marshal(placementPreimage{NetworkID: in.NetworkID, Owner: in.Owner, Database: in.Database, Salt: in.Salt, NodeID: "member-a", I: 0})
	if err != nil || string(pre) != goldenPlacementPreimageJSON {
		t.Fatalf("preimage %s (%v), want %s", pre, err, goldenPlacementPreimageJSON)
	}
	draw := func(node string, i uint32) string {
		t.Helper()
		d, err := PlacementDraw(in.NetworkID, in.Owner, in.Database, in.Salt, node, i)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return d
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		node string
		i    uint32
		want string
	}{{"member-a", 0, goldenPlacementDrawA0}, {"member-b", 0, goldenPlacementDrawB0}, {"member-b", 1, goldenPlacementDrawB1},
		{"member-e", 0, goldenPlacementDrawE0}, {"member-e", 1, goldenPlacementDrawE1}, {"member-e", 2, goldenPlacementDrawE2}} {
		if got := draw(tc.node, tc.i); got != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("draw %s/%d = %s, want %s", tc.node, tc.i, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
	scores := map[string]string{"member-a": goldenPlacementDrawA0, "member-b": goldenPlacementDrawB1, "member-c": goldenPlacementScoreC,
		"member-d": goldenPlacementScoreD, "member-e": goldenPlacementDrawE1}
	p, err := PlaceGroup(in)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var order []string
	for _, s := range p.Order {
		order = append(order, s.NodeID)
		if s.Score != scores[s.NodeID] {
			t.Fatalf("score of %s = %s, want %s", s.NodeID, s.Score, scores[s.NodeID])
		}
		wantSkip := map[string]string{"member-d": "host", "member-e": "failure_domain"}[s.NodeID]
		if s.Skipped != wantSkip || s.Chosen != (wantSkip == "") {
			t.Fatalf("order entry %+v, want skipped %q", s, wantSkip)
		}
	}
	if !slices.Equal(order, goldenPlacementOrder) || !slices.Equal(p.Members, goldenPlacementMembers) || !p.NetworkFill {
		t.Fatalf("placement %+v, want order %v and members %v with fill", p, goldenPlacementOrder, goldenPlacementMembers)
	}
	// The weight rule: with weight 1 member-b scores its first draw and falls
	// below member-a and member-d.
	in.Candidates[1].Weight = 1
	p, err = PlaceGroup(in)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if p.Order[0].NodeID != "member-a" || p.Order[1].NodeID != "member-d" || p.Order[3].NodeID != "member-b" || p.Order[3].Score != goldenPlacementDrawB0 {
		t.Fatalf("weight-1 order %+v", p.Order)
	}
}
```

Create `fsm/placement_test.go` (Step 12 appends the auditor test, which needs the group fixture):

```go
package fsm

import (
	"fmt"
	"math/big"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// TestPlacementScoreIsTheMaxOverWeightDraws: a candidate's score is the
// largest of its weight draws, and comparing draws as strings orders them as
// their 256-bit big-endian values.
func TestPlacementScoreIsTheMaxOverWeightDraws(t *testing.T) {
	in := goldenPlacementInput()
	var draws []string
	for w := uint32(1); w <= 6; w++ {
		best := ""
		for i := uint32(0); i < w; i++ {
			d, err := PlacementDraw(in.NetworkID, in.Owner, in.Database, in.Salt, "member-x", i)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if len(d) != 66 || !strings.HasPrefix(d, "0x") || strings.ToLower(d) != d {
				t.Fatalf("draw %q is not 0x and 64 lowercase hex digits", d)
			}
			draws = append(draws, d)
			if d > best {
				best = d
			}
		}
		got, err := PlacementScoreOf(in.NetworkID, in.Owner, in.Database, in.Salt, "member-x", w)
		if err != nil || got != best {
			t.Fatalf("score at weight %d = %s (%v), want the largest draw %s", w, got, err, best)
		}
	}
	for _, a := range draws {
		for _, b := range draws {
			x, _ := new(big.Int).SetString(a[2:], 16)
			y, _ := new(big.Int).SetString(b[2:], 16)
			if (a < b) != (x.Cmp(y) < 0) {
				t.Fatalf("string order of %s and %s differs from their numeric order", a, b)
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestPlacementSkipsUsedHostsAndFailureDomains: a candidate on the owner's
// host or in its domain is never chosen, and every candidate the walk reaches
// is chosen exactly when neither its host nor its domain is used yet, a used
// host reported before a used domain.
func TestPlacementSkipsUsedHostsAndFailureDomains(t *testing.T) {
	in := PlacementInput{NetworkID: "net-1", Owner: 7, OwnerFailureDomain: "node:o", Database: "dex", Salt: "0x01", GroupSize: 9,
		Candidates: []PlacementCandidate{
			{NodeID: "on-owner-host", HostIndexerID: 7, FailureDomain: "node:x", Weight: 1, Verify: true},
			{NodeID: "in-owner-domain", HostIndexerID: 8, FailureDomain: "node:o", Weight: 1, Verify: true},
			{NodeID: "h9-a", HostIndexerID: 9, FailureDomain: "node:a", Weight: 1, Verify: true},
			{NodeID: "h9-b", HostIndexerID: 9, FailureDomain: "node:b", Weight: 1, Verify: true},
			{NodeID: "h10-a", HostIndexerID: 10, FailureDomain: "node:a", Weight: 1, Verify: true},
			{NodeID: "h11-c", HostIndexerID: 11, FailureDomain: "node:c", Weight: 1, Verify: true},
		}}
	p, err := PlaceGroup(in)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	byNode := map[string]PlacementCandidate{}
	for _, c := range in.Candidates {
		byNode[c.NodeID] = c
	}
	hosts, domains := map[uint64]bool{in.Owner: true}, map[string]bool{in.OwnerFailureDomain: true}
	var chosen []string
	for _, s := range p.Order {
		c := byNode[s.NodeID]
		want := ""
		switch {
		case hosts[c.HostIndexerID]:
			want = "host"
		case domains[c.FailureDomain]:
			want = "failure_domain"
		}
		if s.Skipped != want || s.Chosen != (want == "") {
			t.Fatalf("%s: chosen %v skipped %q, want skipped %q", s.NodeID, s.Chosen, s.Skipped, want)
		}
		if s.Chosen {
			hosts[c.HostIndexerID], domains[c.FailureDomain] = true, true
			chosen = append(chosen, s.NodeID)
		}
	}
	slices.Sort(chosen)
	if !slices.Equal(chosen, p.Members) || slices.Contains(p.Members, "on-owner-host") || slices.Contains(p.Members, "in-owner-domain") || len(p.Members) < 2 {
		t.Fatalf("members %v, chosen in the walk %v", p.Members, chosen)
	}
}

// TestPlacementOrdersEqualScoresByNodeID: ties order by ascending node id.
func TestPlacementOrdersEqualScoresByNodeID(t *testing.T) {
	scores := []PlacementScore{{NodeID: "b", Score: "0x01"}, {NodeID: "c", Score: "0x02"}, {NodeID: "a", Score: "0x01"}}
	orderPlacementScores(scores)
	var got []string
	for _, s := range scores {
		got = append(got, s.NodeID)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(got, []string{"c", "a", "b"}) {
		t.Fatalf("order %v, want [c a b]", got)
	}
}

// TestPlacementForcesFillBelowThreeVerifyMembers: network_fill is the default
// unless fewer than three chosen members verify (spec §6.3).
func TestPlacementForcesFillBelowThreeVerifyMembers(t *testing.T) {
	base := PlacementInput{NetworkID: "net-1", Owner: 0, OwnerFailureDomain: "node:o", Database: "dex", Salt: "0x01", GroupSize: 3}
	for i := uint64(1); i <= 3; i++ {
		base.Candidates = append(base.Candidates, PlacementCandidate{NodeID: fmt.Sprintf("m%d", i), HostIndexerID: i, FailureDomain: fmt.Sprintf("node:%d", i), Weight: 1, Verify: true})
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name      string
		edit      func(*PlacementInput)
		wantFill  bool
		wantCount int
	}{
		{"three verify members, default off", func(*PlacementInput) {}, false, 3},
		{"default on", func(in *PlacementInput) { in.NetworkFillDefault = true }, true, 3},
		{"one replicate-only member", func(in *PlacementInput) { in.Candidates[1].Verify = false }, true, 3},
		{"group of two", func(in *PlacementInput) { in.GroupSize = 2 }, true, 2},
		{"no candidates", func(in *PlacementInput) { in.Candidates = nil }, true, 0},
	} {
		in := base
		in.Candidates = slices.Clone(base.Candidates)
		tc.edit(&in)
		p, err := PlaceGroup(in)
		if err != nil || p.NetworkFill != tc.wantFill || len(p.Members) != tc.wantCount {
			t.Fatalf("%s: placement %+v (%v), want fill %v and %d members", tc.name, p, err, tc.wantFill, tc.wantCount)
		}
	}
}

// TestPlacementRefusesAZeroOrOversizedWeight: the refusals of PlaceGroup,
// verbatim.
func TestPlacementRefusesAZeroOrOversizedWeight(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		edit func(*PlacementInput)
		want string
	}{
		{func(in *PlacementInput) { in.Candidates[0].Weight = 0 }, "placement: weight of member-a must be 1-64, got 0"},
		{func(in *PlacementInput) { in.Candidates[2].Weight = 65 }, "placement: weight of member-c must be 1-64, got 65"},
		{func(in *PlacementInput) { in.GroupSize = 0 }, "placement: group_size must be at least 1"},
		{func(in *PlacementInput) { in.Candidates[3].NodeID = "member-a" }, "placement: candidate member-a is listed twice"},
		{func(in *PlacementInput) { in.Candidates[1].FailureDomain = "" }, "placement: candidate member-b has no failure_domain"},
	} {
		in := goldenPlacementInput()
		tc.edit(&in)
		if _, err := PlaceGroup(in); err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("PlaceGroup = %v, want %q", err, tc.want)
		}
	}
	if _, err := PlacementScoreOf("net-1", 0, "dex", "0x01", "m", 64); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("weight 64 = %v", err)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Recompute the vectors independently**

Contract §49's throwaway check, never committed: it reimplements `replay.CanonicalDigest` with the Python standard library, proves it on the two frozen track headers first, then recomputes every placement vector and compares it with the constant Step 3 froze. Run `mkdir -p -m 700 "$HOME/.cache/s3e3"`, then write `$HOME/.cache/s3e3/goldens.py` with the Write tool (Task 72 recomputes its group-key vectors the same way):

```python
"""Independent recomputation of Plan S3-E3's frozen digests (throwaway, never committed).

Usage: python3 -I goldens.py <arbiter worktree>

It reimplements replay.CanonicalDigest (sha256 over "housegate-replay-mvp-v0:" + domain +
"\\x00" + compact JSON, printed as 0x + 64 lowercase hex) with the standard library only,
checks it first against two frozen L3 header chain hashes, then recomputes every placement
vector of contract section 50 and compares each with the constant the Go test file freezes.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys


def canonical_digest(domain, raw):
    payload = b"housegate-replay-mvp-v0:" + domain.encode() + b"\x00" + raw.encode()
    return "0x" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()


def go_json(obj):
    return json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)


def go_consts(path):
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    consts = {}
    for name, value in re.findall(r'^\s*(golden\w+)\s*=\s*"([^"]*)"', text, re.M):
        consts[name] = value
    for name, value in re.findall(r"^\s*(golden\w+)\s*=\s*`([^`]*)`", text, re.M):
        consts[name] = value
    for name, body in re.findall(r"^\s*(golden\w+)\s*=\s*\[\]string\{([^}]*)\}", text, re.M):
        consts[name] = re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', body)
    return consts


failures = []


def check(label, got, want):
    status = "ok" if got == want else "MISMATCH"
    if got != want:
        failures.append(label)
    print(f"{status} {label} {got}" + ("" if got == want else f" (frozen {want})"))


def main(worktree):
    # 1. The recomputation matches replay.CanonicalDigest on two frozen headers.
    track = go_consts(f"{worktree}/fsm/l3_track_golden_test.go")
    check("goldenTrack1HeaderChainHash",
          canonical_digest("arbiter-l3-header-v1", track["goldenTrack1HeaderJSON"]),
          track["goldenTrack1HeaderChainHash"])
    check("goldenTrack1TransitionHeaderChainHash",
          canonical_digest("arbiter-l3-header-v1", track["goldenTrack1TransitionHeaderJSON"]),
          track["goldenTrack1TransitionHeaderChainHash"])

    # 2. Placement (contract section 50): the fixture of the contract's table.
    frozen = go_consts(f"{worktree}/fsm/placement_golden_test.go")
    net, owner, owner_domain, database = "net-1", 0, "node:o", "dex"
    salt = "0x" + "ab" * 32
    group_size, fill_default = 3, True
    candidates = [  # node id, host, failure domain, weight, verify
        ("member-a", 1, "node:a", 1, True),
        ("member-b", 2, "node:b", 2, True),
        ("member-c", 3, "node:c", 1, True),
        ("member-d", 2, "node:d", 1, True),
        ("member-e", 4, "node:b", 3, False),
    ]

    def preimage(node, i):
        return go_json({"network_id": net, "owner": owner, "database": database, "salt": salt, "node_id": node, "i": i})

    def draw(node, i):
        return canonical_digest("arbiter-group-placement-v1", preimage(node, i))

    def score(node, weight):
        return max(draw(node, i) for i in range(weight))

    check("goldenPlacementPreimageJSON", preimage("member-a", 0), frozen["goldenPlacementPreimageJSON"])
    for label, node, i in [("A0", "member-a", 0), ("B0", "member-b", 0), ("B1", "member-b", 1),
                           ("E0", "member-e", 0), ("E1", "member-e", 1), ("E2", "member-e", 2)]:
        check(f"goldenPlacementDraw{label}", draw(node, i), frozen[f"goldenPlacementDraw{label}"])
    check("goldenPlacementScoreC", score("member-c", 1), frozen["goldenPlacementScoreC"])
    check("goldenPlacementScoreD", score("member-d", 1), frozen["goldenPlacementScoreD"])

    scored = [(score(n, w), n, h, d, v) for n, h, d, w, v in candidates]
    # Descending score as a 256-bit integer, ties by ascending node id.
    order = sorted(scored, key=lambda s: (-int(s[0], 16), s[1]))
    used_hosts, used_domains, chosen, verify = {owner}, {owner_domain}, [], 0
    for s, n, h, d, v in order:
        if len(chosen) == group_size:
            break
        if h in used_hosts or d in used_domains:
            continue
        chosen.append(n)
        used_hosts.add(h)
        used_domains.add(d)
        verify += 1 if v else 0
    check("goldenPlacementOrder", [s[1] for s in order], frozen["goldenPlacementOrder"])
    check("goldenPlacementMembers", sorted(chosen), frozen["goldenPlacementMembers"])
    check("network_fill", fill_default or verify < 3, True)
    # The weight rule: with weight 1 member-b scores its first draw.
    reweighted = sorted([(score(n, 1 if n == "member-b" else w), n) for n, h, d, w, v in candidates],
                        key=lambda s: (-int(s[0], 16), s[1]))
    check("weight-1 order", [n for _, n in reweighted], ["member-a", "member-d", "member-e", "member-b", "member-c"])

    if failures:
        sys.exit("goldens: mismatch in " + ", ".join(failures))
    print("goldens: every value matches")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1])
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Implement the pure placement**

Everything here is a pure function of its arguments and exported, so `arbiter-admin group preview` and an auditor re-derive what Apply places (spec §6.3). Create `fsm/placement.go`:

```go
package fsm

import (
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
)

// Group placement (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §6.3, plan S3-E3 contract §50).
// Everything in this file is a pure function of its arguments, exported so
// arbiter-admin group preview and an auditor re-derive exactly what Apply
// places: the candidates, the salt, the weighted rendezvous scores, the order
// and the chosen members.

// GroupPlacementDomain is the CanonicalDigest domain of one placement draw.
const GroupPlacementDomain = "arbiter-group-placement-v1"

// maxPlacementWeight is the largest weight a candidate may carry (spec §6.1).
const maxPlacementWeight = 64

// PlacementCandidate is one listed member entry placement may choose.
type PlacementCandidate struct {
	NodeID        string
	HostIndexerID uint64
	FailureDomain string
	Weight        uint32
	Verify        bool
}

// PlacementInput is everything one placement reads.
type PlacementInput struct {
	NetworkID          string
	Owner              uint64
	OwnerFailureDomain string
	Database           string
	Salt               string
	GroupSize          uint32
	NetworkFillDefault bool
	Candidates         []PlacementCandidate
}

// PlacementScore is one candidate's place in the walk.
type PlacementScore struct {
	NodeID  string
	Score   string // "0x" + 64 lowercase hex: the largest draw
	Chosen  bool
	Skipped string // "", "host" or "failure_domain"
}

// Placement is the result of one placement.
type Placement struct {
	Members     []string // chosen node ids, ascending
	NetworkFill bool
	Order       []PlacementScore // every candidate, descending Score, ties by ascending NodeID
}

// placementPreimage is the canonical preimage of one draw.
type placementPreimage struct {
	NetworkID string `json:"network_id"`
	Owner     uint64 `json:"owner"`
	Database  string `json:"database"`
	Salt      string `json:"salt"`
	NodeID    string `json:"node_id"`
	I         uint32 `json:"i"`
}

// PlacementDraw is draw i of nodeID: CanonicalDigest over the preimage, "0x"
// and 64 lowercase hex digits.
func PlacementDraw(networkID string, owner uint64, database, salt, nodeID string, i uint32) (string, error) {
	return replay.CanonicalDigest(GroupPlacementDomain, placementPreimage{NetworkID: networkID, Owner: owner, Database: database,
		Salt: salt, NodeID: nodeID, I: i})
}

// PlacementScoreOf is nodeID's score: the largest of its draws 0 … weight-1.
// Draws have one fixed length, so comparing them as strings orders them
// exactly as their 256-bit big-endian values, and the maximum of w uniform
// draws orders candidates as -ln(u)/w does, with no floating point (spec
// §6.3).
func PlacementScoreOf(networkID string, owner uint64, database, salt, nodeID string, weight uint32) (string, error) {
	if weight < 1 || weight > maxPlacementWeight {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("placement: weight of %s must be 1-64, got %d", nodeID, weight)
	}
	best := ""
	for i := uint32(0); i < weight; i++ {
		draw, err := PlacementDraw(networkID, owner, database, salt, nodeID, i)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		if draw > best {
			best = draw
		}
	}
	return best, nil
}

// orderPlacementScores sorts scores by descending Score, ties by ascending
// NodeID.
func orderPlacementScores(scores []PlacementScore) {
	slices.SortFunc(scores, func(a, b PlacementScore) int {
		if c := strings.Compare(b.Score, a.Score); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
		return strings.Compare(a.NodeID, b.NodeID)
	})
}

// PlaceGroup places one group (spec §6.3): candidates in descending score,
// ties by ascending node id, skipping one whose host indexer or failure
// domain the owner or an already chosen member uses, until GroupSize are
// chosen. NetworkFill is NetworkFillDefault, forced on below three verify
// members. A group may be smaller than GroupSize.
func PlaceGroup(in PlacementInput) (Placement, error) {
	if in.GroupSize < 1 {
		return Placement{}, fmt.Errorf("placement: group_size must be at least 1")
	}
	byNode := make(map[string]PlacementCandidate, len(in.Candidates))
	scores := make([]PlacementScore, 0, len(in.Candidates))
	for _, c := range in.Candidates {
		score, err := PlacementScoreOf(in.NetworkID, in.Owner, in.Database, in.Salt, c.NodeID, c.Weight)
		if err != nil {
			return Placement{}, err
		}
		if _, dup := byNode[c.NodeID]; dup {
			return Placement{}, fmt.Errorf("placement: candidate %s is listed twice", c.NodeID)
		}
		if c.FailureDomain == "" {
			return Placement{}, fmt.Errorf("placement: candidate %s has no failure_domain", c.NodeID)
		}
		byNode[c.NodeID] = c
		scores = append(scores, PlacementScore{NodeID: c.NodeID, Score: score})
	}
	orderPlacementScores(scores)
	usedHosts := map[uint64]bool{in.Owner: true}
	usedDomains := map[string]bool{in.OwnerFailureDomain: true}
	var members []string
	verify := 0
	for i := range scores {
		if uint32(len(members)) == in.GroupSize {
			break
		}
		c := byNode[scores[i].NodeID]
		switch {
		case usedHosts[c.HostIndexerID]:
			scores[i].Skipped = "host"
		case usedDomains[c.FailureDomain]:
			scores[i].Skipped = "failure_domain"
		default:
			scores[i].Chosen = true
			usedHosts[c.HostIndexerID] = true
			usedDomains[c.FailureDomain] = true
			members = append(members, c.NodeID)
			if c.Verify {
				verify++
			}
		}
	}
	slices.Sort(members)
	return Placement{Members: members, NetworkFill: in.NetworkFillDefault || verify < 3, Order: scores}, nil
}

// PlacementTarget is one (owner, database) that holds an incarnation with
// physical tables.
type PlacementTarget struct {
	Owner    uint64
	Database string
}

// PlacementTargetsFrom lists, in ascending (owner, database) order, every
// (owner, database) holding an incarnation with physical tables (Pending,
// Active, Retiring or Purging): the databases the placement switch-on
// backfills, restore requires a group for, and group preview previews. An
// incarnation without a recorded owner belongs to foundingIndexer.
func PlacementTargetsFrom(incarnations []*TableIncarnation, foundingIndexer uint64) []PlacementTarget {
	// seen only deduplicates; the sort below fixes the order, so no map
	// order reaches the result.
	seen := map[PlacementTarget]bool{}
	var out []PlacementTarget
	for _, inc := range incarnations {
		if inc == nil || !inc.hasPhysicalTables() {
			continue
		}
		owner := foundingIndexer
		if inc.OwnerIndexerID != nil {
			owner = *inc.OwnerIndexerID
		}
		if target := (PlacementTarget{Owner: owner, Database: inc.DatabaseID}); !seen[target] {
			seen[target] = true
			out = append(out, target)
		}
	}
	slices.SortFunc(out, comparePlacementTargets)
	return out
}

// comparePlacementTargets orders targets by (owner, database).
func comparePlacementTargets(a, b PlacementTarget) int {
	switch {
	case a.Owner < b.Owner:
		return -1
	case a.Owner > b.Owner:
		return 1
	}
	return strings.Compare(a.Database, b.Database)
}

// PlacementCandidatesFrom is the candidate rule of spec §6.3 over explicit
// inputs: every verifiers entry with a host_indexer_id, verify or replicate,
// and a node evicted does not report, whose host is an si_indexers entry other
// than owner and, while excludeQuarantinedHosts, not quarantined. Apply
// (placementCandidatesLocked) and arbiter-admin group preview both call it,
// so the preview cannot drift from Apply.
func PlacementCandidatesFrom(verifiers []arbiter.VerifierEntry, siIndexers []arbiter.SIIndexerEntry, owner uint64, excludeQuarantinedHosts bool,
	evicted func(nodeID string) bool, quarantined func(indexerID uint64) bool) []PlacementCandidate {
	var out []PlacementCandidate
	for _, v := range verifiers {
		if v.HostIndexerID == nil || !(v.Verify || v.Replicate) || evicted(v.NodeID) {
			continue
		}
		host := *v.HostIndexerID
		if host == owner {
			continue
		}
		if _, ok := findSIIndexer(siIndexers, host); !ok {
			continue
		}
		if excludeQuarantinedHosts && quarantined(host) {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, PlacementCandidate{NodeID: v.NodeID, HostIndexerID: host, FailureDomain: v.FailureDomain, Weight: v.Weight, Verify: v.Verify})
	}
	return out
}

// PlacementSaltFrom is the salt rule of plan S3-E1 K61 over explicit inputs:
// the lowest-seq incarnation of (owner, database) that has physical tables
// gives the genesis snapshot id when it is genesis-origin, else its Created
// block hash; with none, created (the AddTable that has not appended yet)
// gives its block hash. An incarnation without a recorded owner belongs to
// foundingIndexer. incarnations are in seq order.
func PlacementSaltFrom(incarnations []*TableIncarnation, foundingIndexer, owner uint64, database, genesisSnapshotID string, created *arbiter.L2EventRef) (string, error) {
	for _, inc := range incarnations {
		if inc == nil || inc.DatabaseID != database || !inc.hasPhysicalTables() {
			continue
		}
		incOwner := foundingIndexer
		if inc.OwnerIndexerID != nil {
			incOwner = *inc.OwnerIndexerID
		}
		if incOwner != owner {
			continue
		}
		if inc.Origin == TableOriginGenesis {
			if genesisSnapshotID == "" {
				return "", fmt.Errorf("placement salt: incarnation %d of %s is genesis-origin and the genesis snapshot id is unknown", inc.Seq, database)
			}
			return genesisSnapshotID, nil
		}
		if inc.Created == nil || inc.Created.BlockHash == "" {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("placement salt: incarnation %d of %s has no created block hash", inc.Seq, database)
		}
		return inc.Created.BlockHash, nil
	}
	if created == nil || created.BlockHash == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("placement salt: database %q of indexer %d has no physical incarnation", database, owner)
	}
	return created.BlockHash, nil
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Write the group FSM tests**

The fixture is `stage3FSM`'s two-owner network with indexers 2 and 3 enrolled, the switches through `owner_aware_selection` on and one listed member entry per host; Tasks 72–75 and Plan S3-E4 reuse its helpers. Create `fsm/stage3_groups_test.go`:

```go
package fsm

import (
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority/authoritytest"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// The groups fixture (plan S3-E3 contract §50) is stage3FSM's two-owner
// network (indexer 1 owns the genesis database db, indexer 0 the chain
// database db0 created at block 150, verifiers v1..v3 the network pool) with
// indexers 2 and 3 enrolled (SNodes s2 and s3, never registered), every
// indexer in its own failure domain node:n<id>, the switches through
// owner_aware_selection on, and one listed member entry per host, member-0 …
// member-3, none registered. groupsFSM turns placement on, which places
// G(0, db0) = {member-1, member-2, member-3} and G(1, db) = {member-0,
// member-2, member-3}, both at generation 1 with fill on.

// groupHostSigner is the enrolment key of indexer host: the tracks fixture's
// keys for indexers 0 and 1, and a key of its own for every host this file
// enrols.
func groupHostSigner(t *testing.T, f *FSM, host uint64) *authority.Signer {
	t.Helper()
	if host <= 1 {
		return hostSigner(t, f, host)
	}
	key := sha256.Sum256([]byte(fmt.Sprintf("stage3 group fixture host key %d", host)))
	return authoritytest.MustSigner(t, hex.EncodeToString(key[:]))
}

// updateStage3 commits stage3Update(t, f) edited by edit.
func updateStage3(t *testing.T, f *FSM, a *authority.Signer, edit func(*arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate)) {
	t.Helper()
	u := stage3Update(t, f)
	edit(&u)
	mustApply(t, f, signedConsensusUpdate(t, a, u))
}

// enrolGroupHosts enrols every indexer of domains (SNode s<id>, never
// registered, activation block 1000+id) with its failure domain, in one
// update.
func enrolGroupHosts(t *testing.T, f *FSM, a *authority.Signer, domains map[uint64]string) {
	t.Helper()
	updateStage3(t, f, a, func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) {
		for _, id := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(domains)) {
			u.SIIndexers = append(u.SIIndexers, siEntry(t, f, groupHostSigner(t, f, id), id, 1000+id, trackSNode(id)))
			u.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains = append(u.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains, arbiter.IndexerFailureDomain{IndexerID: id, FailureDomain: domains[id]})
		}
		u.MaxWriters = uint64(len(u.SIIndexers))
	})
}

// groupMemberEntry is node's member entry on indexer host: every flag true,
// weight 1, the host's committed failure domain, node's own keys and the
// host's consent signed at authoritytest.Iat.
func groupMemberEntry(t *testing.T, f *FSM, host uint64, node string) arbiter.VerifierEntry {
	t.Helper()
	h := host
	entry := arbiter.VerifierEntry{NodeID: node, Ed25519Pubkey: stage3MemberKey(node).Public().(ed25519.PublicKey), HostIndexerID: &h,
		ReplicaSigner: strings.ToLower(stage3ReplicaSigner(t, node).Address()), Weight: 1, FailureDomain: stage3FailureDomain(f.st.Params.Stage3, host),
		Verify: true, Replicate: true, Counts: true, SharedRMT: true}
	entry.ConsentJWS = memberConsent(t, f, groupHostSigner(t, f, host), entry)
	return entry
}

// listGroupMembers lists entries, replacing any entry of the same node.
func listGroupMembers(t *testing.T, f *FSM, a *authority.Signer, entries ...arbiter.VerifierEntry) {
	t.Helper()
	updateStage3(t, f, a, func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) {
		for _, e := range entries {
			*u = withVerifier(*u, e)
		}
	})
}

// groupsReadyFSM is the groups fixture before the placement switch.
func groupsReadyFSM(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer) {
	t.Helper()
	f, a := stage3FSM(t)
	enrolGroupHosts(t, f, a, map[uint64]string{2: "node:n2", 3: "node:n3"})
	turnOnStage3SwitchesThrough(t, f, a, Stage3SwitchOwnerAwareSelection)
	var entries []arbiter.VerifierEntry
	for host := uint64(0); host <= 3; host++ {
		entries = append(entries, groupMemberEntry(t, f, host, stage3TestMember(host)))
	}
	listGroupMembers(t, f, a, entries...)
	return f, a
}

// groupsFSM is the groups fixture with placement on.
func groupsFSM(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer) {
	t.Helper()
	f, a := groupsReadyFSM(t)
	turnOnStage3Switch(t, f, a, Stage3SwitchPlacement)
	return f, a
}

// mustGroup is G(owner, database), which must exist.
func mustGroup(t *testing.T, f *FSM, owner uint64, database string) *DatabaseGroup {
	t.Helper()
	g := f.groupLocked(owner, database)
	if g == nil {
		t.Fatalf("no group for indexer %d database %q", owner, database)
	}
	return g
}

// rebalanceCmd is RebalanceGroup carrying add and remove as given, signed by
// signer over its canonical form under f's current context at
// authoritytest.Iat.
func rebalanceCmd(t *testing.T, f *FSM, signer *authority.Signer, owner uint64, database string, generation uint64, add, remove []string, fill bool) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := wire.RebalanceGroup{OwnerIndexerID: owner, DatabaseID: database, ExpectedGeneration: generation, Add: add, Remove: remove, NetworkFill: fill}
	token, err := signer.SignRebalanceGroupWithContextAt(cmd.Canonical(), authorityContextFor(t, f), authoritytest.Iat)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cmd.AuthorityJWS = token
	return wire.Command{RebalanceGroup: &cmd}
}

// registryVersion is f's committed table registry version.
func registryVersion(f *FSM) uint64 { return f.st.TableRegistry.Version }

// rejectGroupCommand applies cmd, requires the refusal want (or, with
// prefix, a refusal starting with want), and requires the snapshot and the
// registry version unchanged.
func rejectGroupCommand(t *testing.T, f *FSM, cmd wire.Command, want string, prefix bool) {
	t.Helper()
	before, version := snapshotBytes(t, f), registryVersion(f)
	got := applyExpectReject(t, f, cmd).Reason
	if got != want && !(prefix && strings.HasPrefix(got, want)) {
		t.Fatalf("refusal %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(before, snapshotBytes(t, f)) || registryVersion(f) != version {
		t.Fatal("a refused command changed state")
	}
}

// registerMember registers member node at registration seq 1, signed by its
// fixture key, so it can report purges and be evicted.
func registerMember(t *testing.T, f *FSM, node string) {
	t.Helper()
	key := stage3MemberKey(node)
	reg := wire.RegistrationFromPB(wire.RegistrationToPB(arbiter.NodeRegistration{NodeID: node, Roles: []arbiter.NodeRole{arbiter.NodeRoleVerifier},
		Ed25519Pubkey: key.Public().(ed25519.PublicKey), RegistrationSeq: 1}))
	sig, err := authority.SignVerifierMessage(key, authority.VerifierMessageRegistration, messageContextFor(t, f), reg)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	mustApply(t, f, wire.Command{RegisterNode: &wire.RegisterNode{Registration: reg, Ed25519Signature: sig}})
}

// memberPurged is member node's purge report for incarnation seq.
func memberPurged(t *testing.T, f *FSM, node string, seq uint64) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	sig, err := authority.SignVerifierMessage(stage3MemberKey(node), authority.VerifierMessageTablePurged, messageContextFor(t, f),
		authority.TablePurgedBody{NodeID: node, IncarnationSeq: seq})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return wire.Command{RecordTablePurged: &wire.RecordTablePurged{NodeID: node, IncarnationSeq: seq, Ed25519Signature: sig}}
}

// evictCmd is the authority eviction of node at its registration seq.
func evictCmd(t *testing.T, f *FSM, a *authority.Signer, node string, seq uint64) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := arbiter.EvictNodeCommand{NodeID: node, ExpectedRegistrationSeq: seq, Reason: "decommissioned"}
	token, err := a.SignEvictNodeWithContextAt(cmd, authorityContextFor(t, f), authoritytest.Iat)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return wire.Command{EvictNode: &wire.EvictNode{NodeID: node, ExpectedRegistrationSeq: seq, Reason: cmd.Reason, AuthorityJWS: token}}
}

// addGroupTable adds database.table owned by owner, created at block (hash
// "0x<block>") with its schema at block+1, and returns its incarnation seq.
func addGroupTable(t *testing.T, f *FSM, owner uint64, database, table string, block uint64) uint64 {
	t.Helper()
	mustApply(t, f, ownedAddCmd(t, f, database, table, ev(block, fmt.Sprintf("0x%d", block), 0), ev(block+1, fmt.Sprintf("0x%d", block+1), 0), owner))
	return f.st.TableRegistry.Live(arbiter.TableKey(database, table)).Seq
}

// purgeByOwnerAndPool retires database.table at block (a Pending incarnation
// without a sealed add retires straight to Purging) and applies the purge
// reports of indexer 1's SNode s1 and the pool verifiers v1..v3.
func purgeByOwnerAndPool(t *testing.T, f *FSM, database, table string, block uint64, seq uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	mustApply(t, f, retireCmd(database, wire.TableRetireReasonTableDeleted, ev(block, fmt.Sprintf("0x%d", block), 0), table))
	mustApply(t, f, snodePurged(t, f, indexerSigner1(t), "s1", seq))
	for _, v := range []string{"v1", "v2", "v3"} {
		mustApply(t, f, verifierPurged(t, f, v, v[len(v)-1], seq))
	}
}

// expectedPlacement is PlaceGroup over f's committed parameters for
// (owner, database) with salt, the auditor's re-derivation.
func expectedPlacement(t *testing.T, f *FSM, owner uint64, database, salt string) Placement {
	t.Helper()
	p, err := PlaceGroup(PlacementInput{NetworkID: f.st.Params.NetworkID, Owner: owner, OwnerFailureDomain: stage3FailureDomain(f.st.Params.Stage3, owner),
		Database: database, Salt: salt, GroupSize: f.st.Params.Stage3.GroupSize, NetworkFillDefault: f.st.Params.Stage3.NetworkFillDefault,
		Candidates: f.placementCandidatesLocked(f.st.Params, owner)})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return p
}

// setMemberClass stands in for Plan S3-E3 Task 75's checkpoints, the only
// Apply path that moves a member out of bootstrapping.
func setMemberClass(t *testing.T, g *DatabaseGroup, node string, class MemberClass) {
	t.Helper()
	i := groupMemberIndex(g, node)
	if i < 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%s is not a member", node)
	}
	g.Members[i].Class = class
}

// forgedGroupsSnapshot restores f's snapshot into a bare replica, applies
// mutate to its state and snapshots it again, so the forgery is written by
// the same writer as an honest container.
func forgedGroupsSnapshot(t *testing.T, f *FSM, mutate func(st *State)) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	g := restoreInto(t, snapshotBytes(t, f))
	mutate(g.st)
	return snapshotBytes(t, g)
}

func TestAddTablePlacesAGroupForTheFirstPhysicalIncarnation(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := groupsFSM(t)
	version := registryVersion(f)
	seq := addGroupTable(t, f, 1, "dbn", "a", 200)
	g := mustGroup(t, f, 1, "dbn")
	want := expectedPlacement(t, f, 1, "dbn", "0x200")
	if g.Generation != 1 || g.Salt != "0x200" || !slices.Equal(groupMemberIDs(g), want.Members) || g.NetworkFill != want.NetworkFill ||
		!slices.Equal(want.Members, []string{"member-0", "member-2", "member-3"}) {
		t.Fatalf("group %+v, want generation 1, salt 0x200 and placement %+v", g, want)
	}
	for _, m := range g.Members {
		if m.JoinedGeneration != 1 || m.Class != MemberBootstrapping {
			t.Fatalf("member %+v, want joined at 1 and bootstrapping", m)
		}
	}
	if inc := f.st.TableRegistry.incarnation(seq); !slices.Equal(inc.PurgeMembers, want.Members) {
		t.Fatalf("purge_members %v, want %v", inc.PurgeMembers, want.Members)
	}
	if got := registryVersion(f); got != version+1 {
		t.Fatalf("registry version %d, want one bump from %d", got, version)
	}
	// The second table of the database joins the group; nothing is placed
	// again.
	second := addGroupTable(t, f, 1, "dbn", "b", 210)
	if again := mustGroup(t, f, 1, "dbn"); again != g || g.Generation != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("a second incarnation re-placed the group: %+v", again)
	}
	if inc := f.st.TableRegistry.incarnation(second); !slices.Equal(inc.PurgeMembers, want.Members) {
		t.Fatalf("second purge_members %v", inc.PurgeMembers)
	}
}

func TestAddTableOfARefusedIncarnationPlacesNoGroup(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := groupsFSM(t)
	mustApply(t, f, ownedAddCmd(t, f, "dbr", "a.b", ev(200, "0x200", 0), ev(201, "0x201", 0), 1))
	inc := f.st.TableRegistry.Live("dbr.a.b")
	if inc == nil || inc.Status != TableStatusRefused || len(inc.PurgeMembers) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("incarnation %+v, want Refused without purge_members", inc)
	}
	// Not even transiently: a group placed and dropped again in the same
	// Apply would leave its durable generation behind.
	if f.groupLocked(1, "dbr") != nil || f.groupGenerationLocked(1, "dbr") != 0 || len(f.st.Stage3.GroupGenerations) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("a Refused incarnation placed a group: groups %d, generations %+v", len(f.st.Stage3.Groups), f.st.Stage3.GroupGenerations)
	}
}

func TestAddTableBeforePlacementPlacesNoGroup(t *testing.T) {
```
