## Task 74: arbiter — `ReselectVerifiers` (tag 39): the latched refusal, evidence deletion, the cursor timeout and ring-ordered replacements (S3-E3)

Spec §7.4 (re-selection: a verifier without complete evidence is replaced when it is evicted, no longer eligible or timed out on the committed L2 registry cursor, one with complete evidence only when evicted; replacements walk the stored ring after the stored position; at most ring size − 3 re-selections; refused after the latch or on a challenged statement; replaced verifiers' evidence ignored; the proof and its epoch stored; restore checks the records structurally, the latch count and the proof under its epoch, without re-deriving node status), §10.4 switch 7 (`reselection`) and §17 (re-selection on a quiet track and its restore checks; two passes latch, one passing verifier is evicted, a re-selection is refused and a snapshot/restore keeps the verdict), as fixed by contract §52.2 and clarification K75. With the switch on, the WorkSet lists every block a re-selection would be applied for in `ReselectionDue`, the leader's orchestrator signs `ReselectVerifiers{l3_block_seq, expected_set}` with its authority signer and proposes it, and Apply replaces the verifiers, deletes their evidence, appends a `Reselection` record and re-evaluates the block; the verdict that latches records the block's re-selection count; `GetBlockVerification` serves the records without their signed expected set (D33); the node-local counter `arbiter_verifier_reselections_total` counts the applied commands. Before the switch Apply refuses tag 39 first, the row is empty, the orchestrator proposes nothing and no new field is written (all `omitempty`), so every Apply, snapshot and chain hash is byte for byte the branch's after Task 73.

Notes:
- **One predicate for Apply and the WorkSet.** Refusals 7–11 (latched, challenged, the ring limit, no replaceable verifier, no replacement) live in `reselectionPlanLocked`, which Apply calls after the shape, block, authority and expected-set checks and which `reselectionDueLocked` calls for the WorkSet row. A row is listed exactly when the signed command over its `ExpectedSet` would be applied, so the orchestrator never proposes a command Apply refuses (`TestWorkSetListsReselectionDueWithTheApplyPredicate`), and an `ErrRejected` only means the block changed between the read and the proposal. The row is computed on every WorkSet read and stores nothing.
- **Replaceable.** A verifier of the set is replaceable when it is `NodeEvicted` (whatever its evidence), or when its attestation or scan is missing and it is either out of `eligibleRingLocked(owner, bv.SourceNodes, bv.groupSeal())` now (Task 73's filter: delisted, Syncing, removed from the group, owner-hosted, quarantined host) or timed out. The timeout counts from the larger of `MarkedCursorBlock` and the last `Reselection.CursorBlock` (K75; the two are equal in practice, because the cursor only advances) and fires when the committed registry cursor is `evidence_timeout_l2_blocks` past it. The table-registry watcher advances the cursor every `cursor_advance_interval` whatever the track's traffic, so a quiet track times out too (`TestReselectVerifiersOnAQuietTrackFiresOnTheRegistryCursor`). With eviction voiding on (implied by placement), an evicted verifier's evidence is already out of the verdict (Plan S3-E2 Task 68), so deleting it changes no verdict.
- **The walk and the limit.** Replacements walk the stored ring from `RingPosition + 1` cyclically, at most once around, one per replaced verifier in sorted order, skipping a node in the current set, one an earlier re-selection of the block replaced (even when it is eligible again) and one not in the eligible ring now; `RingPosition` moves to the last node taken. `Replacements` is stored in that walk order, as contract §52.2 fixes; Plan S3-E1's comment on `BlockReselection` calls both lists sorted, which holds for `replaced` and for a single replacement, and the server serves the stored order (recorded for the consistency pass). A block is re-selected at most `len(EligibleRing) − 3` times; a block marked before `owner_aware_selection` stores no ring, so its limit is 0 and refusal 9 answers it: such a block can only latch on its own set, so Plan S3-F's runbook should confirm, before switch 7, that every block marked before the `owner_aware_selection` cutover has latched (recorded as an open question).
- **Evidence deletion (K75).** The replaced verifiers' `Attestations`, `ByteScans` and `Verdict.Replicas` entries are deleted in the same Apply, before `reevaluateBlock` recomputes the verdict over the new set. Late evidence of a replaced verifier is refused by the existing set check (`replica not in the block's verifier set`), and restore can require every evidence key of a stage-3-marked block to name a member of its set. Deleting `Verdict.Replicas` is defensive: `reevaluateBlock` rebuilds the map from the set whenever the block is evaluable.
- **The latch.** `reevaluateBlock` sets `ReselectionsAtLatch = len(bv.Reselections)` when the quorum latches. A block never re-selected records 0, which `omitempty` drops, so every verdict before the switch keeps its bytes. A latched block is never re-evaluated (`reevaluateBlock`'s guard), so the count is final, and a re-selection after the latch is refused by refusal 7 and by restore.
- **Restore.** `validateStage3Selection` (Task 70) now checks the marking's position and set: for a re-selected block those are the block-seeded position and the first record's `ExpectedSet`. `validateStage3Reselections` then checks, per block: the switch (a record with the switch off is refused, `carries re-selections while the reselection switch is off`, added); the ring limit; each record's shape against the stored ring, the previous position and cursor block, and the ids earlier records replaced; the chain from record to record to the stored set and position; the latch count (a latched verdict must record exactly the stored count, an unlatched one none, the second text added); and evidence keys inside the set, for every block marked from a ring or re-selected (blocks marked before `owner_aware_selection` keep today's rules, so no older container gains a refusal). `validateReselectionProofs` re-verifies every proof under the authority set and `{network, genesis, epoch}` of its stored `AuthorityEpoch`, refusing an epoch beyond the history. Node status is never re-derived (spec §7.4). `validateLatchedConsensus` runs unchanged over the final set.
- **Orchestrator.** `handleReselections` runs from `handleWorkSet` after `handleDispatchRows`, signs each row with `SignReselectVerifiersWithContext` under `authoritySigningContext`, logs the row at info level, and ignores `ErrRejected`. A signing failure is logged and the row skipped, as cleanup signing does; a missing signer or an authority set without it pauses the work with the existing warnings. There is no operator RPC (K75).
- **The counter.** `reselectionsApplied` is node-local state of the FSM struct (guarded by `mu`, never snapshotted, kept across a `Restore`, like `registryWake`), so it never reaches a digest. The collector reads it through the optional `reselectionReader`, as it reads `stateSizeReader`; `*fsm.FSM` implements both and `cmd/arbiter` already passes the FSM, so no wiring changes. Plan S3-E4 Task 80 owns the alerting rule and Task 81 the README; this task changes no README.
- **Fixture.** The tests use Plan S3-E2's `ownerAwareFSM` with the pool extended to `v<ring>` and the placement and reselection switches committed. No host-bound entry is listed, so both placed groups have no member and `network_fill` on, every block's eligible ring is the Active pool minus its source (Task 73's group half adds no member), and "no longer eligible" is exercised with a pool verifier back in Syncing (a registered, non-evicted verifier cannot be delisted, `signedClaimsMembershipLocked` rule 6). The group half of the filter is Task 73's and is pinned by its tests; this task only calls it.
- **Frozen fixtures.** No golden or vector file changes; `TestStage3V21PlainContainerGolden` and `TestStage3V21InternedContainerGolden` are captured with every switch off and carry no new field, so they stay byte-identical (Step 13).

// entry is listed, so both placed groups have no member and network_fill on,
// and a block of indexer 1 (source s1) draws its set from the whole pool
// ring. evidence_timeout_l2_blocks is the fixture's 30. The helpers carry the
// suffix RS so they never collide with another task's.

// reselectionFSM is the fixture with a pool of ring verifiers (3 to 9).
func reselectionFSM(t *testing.T, ring int) (*FSM, *authority.Signer) {
	t.Helper()
	f, a := reselectionOffFSM(t, ring)
	turnOnStage3Switch(t, f, a, Stage3SwitchReselection)
	return f, a
}

// reselectionOffFSM is reselectionFSM with the reselection switch still off.
func reselectionOffFSM(t *testing.T, ring int) (*FSM, *authority.Signer) {
	t.Helper()
	if ring < VerifierSelectN || ring > 9 {
		t.Fatalf("a pool of %d verifiers is outside 3..9", ring)
	}
	f, a := ownerAwareFSM(t)
	var ids []string
	for i := VerifierSelectN + 1; i <= ring; i++ {
		ids = append(ids, fmt.Sprintf("v%d", i))
	}
	if len(ids) > 0 {
		addPoolVerifiersOA(t, f, a, ids...)
	}
	turnOnStage3Switch(t, f, a, Stage3SwitchPlacement)
	return f, a
}

// markedBlockRS admits the fixed client's statement seq for indexer 1, seals
// it alone, binds its claim and marks the block replaying from the pool ring.
func markedBlockRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, seq uint64) uint64 {
	t.Helper()
	key, account := fixedClient(t)
	block := claimedBlockOA(t, f, key, account, seq, 1)
	markReplayingOA(t, f, block)
	if len(f.st.Verifications[block].EligibleRing) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("block %d was marked without an eligible ring", block)
	}
	return block
}

// verifiersRS is a copy of block's current verifier set.
func verifiersRS(f *FSM, block uint64) []string {
	return slices.Clone(f.st.Verifications[block].VerifierSet)
}

// evidenceRS is replica rid's passing attestation and byte-side scan of the
// marked block: pinnedEvidence's receipt and scan signed with rid's key.
func evidenceRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, block uint64, rid string) (wire.Command, wire.Command) {
	t.Helper()
	cmds := pinnedEvidence(t, f, block)
	receipt := cmds[0].RecordAttestation.Attestation.Receipt
	parts := cmds[1].RecordByteSideScan.Scan.Parts
	seed := rid[len(rid)-1]
	return wire.Command{RecordAttestation: &wire.RecordAttestation{Attestation: signedAttestation(t, rid, seed, receipt)}},
		wire.Command{RecordByteSideScan: &wire.RecordByteSideScan{Scan: signedScan(t, rid, seed, block, parts)}}
}

// passRS records rid's complete, passing evidence for block.
func passRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, block uint64, rid string) {
	t.Helper()
	att, scan := evidenceRS(t, f, block, rid)
	mustApply(t, f, att)
	mustApply(t, f, scan)
}

// attestRS records only rid's attestation, so its evidence stays incomplete.
func attestRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, block uint64, rid string) {
	t.Helper()
	att, _ := evidenceRS(t, f, block, rid)
	mustApply(t, f, att)
}

// reselectRS is block's ReselectVerifiers over expected, signed by a at
// authoritytest.Iat in f's current authority context.
func reselectRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, a *authority.Signer, block uint64, expected []string) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := wire.ReselectVerifiers{L3BlockSeq: block, ExpectedSet: slices.Clone(expected)}
	token, err := a.SignReselectVerifiersWithContextAt(cmd.Canonical(), authorityContextFor(t, f), authoritytest.Iat)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cmd.AuthorityJWS = token
	return wire.Command{ReselectVerifiers: &cmd}
}

// reselectSetRS is reselectRS over block's current set.
func reselectSetRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, a *authority.Signer, block uint64) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	return reselectRS(t, f, a, block, verifiersRS(f, block))
}

// unsignedReselectRS is a ReselectVerifiers whose token no refusal before the
// authority check reads.
func unsignedReselectRS(block uint64, expected []string) wire.Command {
	return wire.Command{ReselectVerifiers: &wire.ReselectVerifiers{L3BlockSeq: block, ExpectedSet: expected, AuthorityJWS: "e30.e30.c2ln"}}
}

// authorityRefusalRS is Apply's refusal of c's token: the validator's own
// error under f's current authorities and context.
func authorityRefusalRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, c wire.Command) string {
	t.Helper()
	r := c.ReselectVerifiers
	v := &authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: authorityAddressSet(f.st.Params.AuthorityAddresses)}
	_, err := v.VerifyReselectVerifiers(r.Canonical(), r.AuthorityJWS, authorityContextFor(t, f))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("the token verifies")
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers block %d: authority: %v", r.L3BlockSeq, err)
}

// cursorRS advances the committed registry cursor to L2 block to.
func cursorRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, to uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	if to > f.st.TableRegistry.Cursor.BlockNumber {
		mustApply(t, f, advanceTo(to))
	}
	if got := f.st.TableRegistry.Cursor.BlockNumber; got != to {
		t.Fatalf("registry cursor = %d, want %d", got, to)
	}
}

// sinceRS is the cursor block block's timeout counts from: its last
// re-selection's, else its marking's.
func sinceRS(f *FSM, block uint64) uint64 {
	bv := f.st.Verifications[block]
	if n := len(bv.Reselections); n > 0 {
		return bv.Reselections[n-1].CursorBlock
	}
	return bv.MarkedCursorBlock
}

// timeOutRS advances the cursor exactly evidence_timeout_l2_blocks past
// sinceRS.
func timeOutRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, block uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	cursorRS(t, f, sinceRS(f, block)+f.st.Params.Stage3.EvidenceTimeoutL2Blocks)
}

// regSeqRS is node id's current registration seq.
func regSeqRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, id string) uint64 {
	t.Helper()
	n := f.st.Nodes[id]
	if n == nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s is not registered", id)
	}
	return n.Registration.RegistrationSeq
}

// evictRS evicts verifier id at its current registration seq.
func evictRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, a *authority.Signer, id string) {
	t.Helper()
	evictVerifierOA(t, f, a, id, regSeqRS(t, f, id))
}

// resyncRS re-registers verifier id at its next registration seq: it is
// Syncing, so it is in no eligible ring until reactivateRS.
func resyncRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, id string) {
	t.Helper()
	resyncVerifierOA(t, f, id, regSeqRS(t, f, id)+1)
}

// reactivateRS marks verifier id Active again at its current registration seq.
func reactivateRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, id string) {
	t.Helper()
	reactivateVerifierOA(t, f, id, regSeqRS(t, f, id))
}

// replaceableRS is replaceableVerifiersLocked of block now.
func replaceableRS(f *FSM, block uint64) []string {
	f.mu.RLock()
	defer f.mu.RUnlock()
	return f.replaceableVerifiersLocked(block, f.st.Verifications[block])
}

// dueRS is block's WorkSet.ReselectionDue row.
func dueRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, block uint64) (ReselectionWork, bool) {
	t.Helper()
	ws, err := f.WorkSet()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, row := range ws.ReselectionDue {
		if row.BlockSeq == block {
			return row, true
		}
	}
	return ReselectionWork{}, false
}

// lastReselectionRS is block's newest stored re-selection.
func lastReselectionRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, block uint64) Reselection {
	t.Helper()
	rs := f.st.Verifications[block].Reselections
	if len(rs) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("block %d has no re-selection", block)
	}
	return rs[len(rs)-1]
}

// ringAtRS is the node at position p, taken cyclically, of block's stored
// ring.
func ringAtRS(f *FSM, block uint64, p int) string {
	ring := f.st.Verifications[block].EligibleRing
	return ring[((p%len(ring))+len(ring))%len(ring)]
}

// outsideRS is the stored ring of block minus its current set, in ring order.
func outsideRS(f *FSM, block uint64) []string {
	bv := f.st.Verifications[block]
	var out []string
	for _, id := range bv.EligibleRing {
		if !slices.Contains(bv.VerifierSet, id) {
			out = append(out, id)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// requireReselectedRS requires block's newest re-selection to have replaced
// replaced, and the set to be the previous one with them swapped out.
func requireReselectedRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, block uint64, before, replaced []string) Reselection {
	t.Helper()
	r := lastReselectionRS(t, f, block)
	want := slices.DeleteFunc(slices.Clone(before), func(id string) bool { return slices.Contains(replaced, id) })
	want = append(want, r.Replacements...)
	slices.Sort(want)
	if !slices.Equal(r.ExpectedSet, before) || !slices.Equal(r.Replaced, replaced) || len(r.Replacements) != len(replaced) ||
		!slices.Equal(verifiersRS(f, block), want) || f.st.Verifications[block].RingPosition != r.RingPosition {
		t.Fatalf("re-selection %+v over %v, set now %v; want %v replaced", r, before, verifiersRS(f, block), replaced)
	}
	return r
}

// TestReselectVerifiersRefusals: contract §52.2. Every refusal, in order,
// leaves state unchanged.
func TestReselectVerifiersRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	type built struct {
		f      *FSM
		cmd    wire.Command
		reason string
	}
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		build func(t *testing.T) built
	}{
		{"1 the reselection switch is off", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionOffFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			return built{f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block), "re-selection is refused until the reselection switch is on"}
		}},
		{"2 two ids", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, _ := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			set := verifiersRS(f, markedBlockRS(t, f, 1))
			return built{f, unsignedReselectRS(2, set[:2]), "reselect verifiers: expected_set must be 3 sorted unique node ids"}
		}},
		{"2 four ids", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, _ := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			return built{f, unsignedReselectRS(2, []string{"v1", "v2", "v3", "v4"}), "reselect verifiers: expected_set must be 3 sorted unique node ids"}
		}},
		{"2 unsorted", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, _ := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			set := verifiersRS(f, markedBlockRS(t, f, 1))
			return built{f, unsignedReselectRS(2, []string{set[1], set[0], set[2]}), "reselect verifiers: expected_set must be 3 sorted unique node ids"}
		}},
		{"2 repeated", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, _ := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			set := verifiersRS(f, markedBlockRS(t, f, 1))
			return built{f, unsignedReselectRS(2, []string{set[0], set[0], set[1]}), "reselect verifiers: expected_set must be 3 sorted unique node ids"}
		}},
		{"2 an empty id", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, _ := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			set := verifiersRS(f, markedBlockRS(t, f, 1))
			return built{f, unsignedReselectRS(2, []string{"", set[0], set[1]}), "reselect verifiers: expected_set must be 3 sorted unique node ids"}
		}},
		{"3 a block beyond the sealed tip", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, _ := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			set := verifiersRS(f, markedBlockRS(t, f, 1))
			return built{f, unsignedReselectRS(99, set), "reselect verifiers: unknown block 99"}
		}},
		{"3 block 0", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, _ := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			set := verifiersRS(f, markedBlockRS(t, f, 1))
			return built{f, unsignedReselectRS(0, set), "reselect verifiers: unknown block 0"}
		}},
		{"4 a sealed, unmarked block", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, _ := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			key, account := fixedClient(t)
			block := claimedBlockOA(t, f, key, account, 1, 1)
			return built{f, unsignedReselectRS(block, []string{"v1", "v2", "v3"}), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d is not marked replaying", block)}
		}},
		{"5 a token of a key outside the authorities", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			other, _ := authorityFixture(t)
			cmd := reselectSetRS(t, f, other, block)
			return built{f, cmd, authorityRefusalRS(t, f, cmd)}
		}},
		{"5 a token of another block", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			cmd := reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block)
			cmd.ReselectVerifiers.AuthorityJWS = reselectRS(t, f, a, block+1, verifiersRS(f, block)).ReselectVerifiers.AuthorityJWS
			return built{f, cmd, authorityRefusalRS(t, f, cmd)}
		}},
		{"5 a token of an earlier epoch", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			cmd := reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block)
			addPoolVerifiersOA(t, f, a, "v7")
			return built{f, cmd, authorityRefusalRS(t, f, cmd)}
		}},
		{"6 an expected set that is not the block's", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			set := verifiersRS(f, block)
			evictRS(t, f, a, set[0])
			other := append([]string{outsideRS(f, block)[0]}, set[1:]...)
			slices.Sort(other)
			return built{f, reselectRS(t, f, a, block, other), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: expected_set differs from the verifier set of block %d", block)}
		}},
		{"7 a latched quorum", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			set := verifiersRS(f, block)
			passRS(t, f, block, set[0])
			passRS(t, f, block, set[1])
			timeOutRS(t, f, block)
			return built{f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d quorum has latched", block)}
		}},
		{"8 a challenged statement", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			timeOutRS(t, f, block)
			mustApply(t, f, wire.Command{OpenChallenge: &wire.OpenChallenge{BlockSeq: block, Reason: "operator review", OpenedBy: "test"}})
			return built{f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d has a challenged statement", block)}
		}},
		{"9 the ring's limit", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 4)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			return built{f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d was re-selected 1 times, the limit for its ring of 4", block)}
		}},
		{"10 no replaceable verifier", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			cursorRS(t, f, sinceRS(f, block)+f.st.Params.Stage3.EvidenceTimeoutL2Blocks-1)
			return built{f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d has no replaceable verifier", block)}
		}},
		{"11 no replacement", func(t *testing.T) built {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 4)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			set := verifiersRS(f, block)
			evictRS(t, f, a, set[0])
			evictRS(t, f, a, set[1])
			return built{f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d has no replacement for %s", block, set[1])}
		}},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			b := tc.build(t)
			rejectStage3Unchanged(t, b.f, b.cmd, b.reason)
		})
	}
}

// TestReselectVerifiersReplacesOnlyIncompleteEvictedIneligibleOrTimedOut:
// spec §7.4, contract §52.2. A verifier without complete evidence (none, or
// an attestation alone) is replaced once it is evicted, out of the block's
// eligible ring or timed out on the committed registry cursor, and not
// before.
func TestReselectVerifiersReplacesOnlyIncompleteEvictedIneligibleOrTimedOut(t *testing.T) {
	setup := func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64, []string) {
		t.Helper()
		f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 7)
		block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
		set := verifiersRS(f, block)
		attestRS(t, f, block, set[0])
		cursorRS(t, f, sinceRS(f, block)+f.st.Params.Stage3.EvidenceTimeoutL2Blocks-1)
		if got := replaceableRS(f, block); got != nil {
			t.Fatalf("replaceable before any reason = %v", got)
		}
		rejectStage3Unchanged(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d has no replaceable verifier", block))
		return f, a, block, set
	}
	t.Run("evicted", func(t *testing.T) {
		f, a, block, set := setup(t)
		evictRS(t, f, a, set[1])
		if got := replaceableRS(f, block); !slices.Equal(got, set[1:2]) {
			t.Fatalf("replaceable = %v, want %v", got, set[1:2])
		}
		mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
		requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, set, set[1:2])
	})
	t.Run("no longer eligible", func(t *testing.T) {
		f, a, block, set := setup(t)
		resyncRS(t, f, set[0])
		if got := replaceableRS(f, block); !slices.Equal(got, set[:1]) {
			t.Fatalf("replaceable = %v, want %v (its attestation alone is incomplete)", got, set[:1])
		}
		mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
		requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, set, set[:1])
	})
	t.Run("timed out", func(t *testing.T) {
		f, a, block, set := setup(t)
		timeOutRS(t, f, block)
		if got := replaceableRS(f, block); !slices.Equal(got, set) {
			t.Fatalf("replaceable = %v, want the whole set %v", got, set)
		}
		mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
		if r := requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, set, set); r.CursorBlock != f.st.TableRegistry.Cursor.BlockNumber {
			t.Fatalf("cursor block = %d, want the committed cursor %d", r.CursorBlock, f.st.TableRegistry.Cursor.BlockNumber)
		}
	})
}

// TestAVerifierWithCompleteEvidenceIsReplacedOnlyIfEvicted: spec §7.4. A
// verifier whose attestation and scan are both recorded stays through a
// timeout and through leaving the eligible ring, and is replaced once
// evicted, whose evidence eviction voiding already dropped from the verdict.
func TestAVerifierWithCompleteEvidenceIsReplacedOnlyIfEvicted(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 7)
	block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
	set := verifiersRS(f, block)
	passRS(t, f, block, set[0])
	timeOutRS(t, f, block)
	resyncRS(t, f, set[0])
	if got := replaceableRS(f, block); !slices.Equal(got, set[1:]) {
		t.Fatalf("replaceable = %v, want %v: complete evidence protects %s", got, set[1:], set[0])
	}
	mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
	requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, set, set[1:])
	if bv := f.st.Verifications[block]; bv.Attestations[set[0]] == nil || bv.ByteScans[set[0]] == nil || !bv.Verdict.Replicas[set[0]].Pass {
		t.Fatalf("%s's evidence did not survive the re-selection: %+v", set[0], bv.Verdict)
	}
	if got := replaceableRS(f, block); got != nil {
		t.Fatalf("replaceable right after the re-selection = %v", got)
	}
	before := verifiersRS(f, block)
	evictRS(t, f, a, set[0])
	if got := replaceableRS(f, block); !slices.Equal(got, set[:1]) {
		t.Fatalf("replaceable after the eviction = %v, want %v", got, set[:1])
	}
	mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
	requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, before, set[:1])
	if bv := f.st.Verifications[block]; bv.Attestations[set[0]] != nil || bv.ByteScans[set[0]] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the evicted verifier's evidence stayed: %v", slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(bv.Attestations)))
	}
}

// TestReplacementsFollowTheStoredRingAfterTheRingPosition: spec §7.4,
// contract §52.2. Each replacement is the next node of the ring stored at the
// marking after the stored position, skipping a node in the set, one an
// earlier re-selection replaced (even when it is eligible again) and one that
// is not eligible now, and the position moves to the last node taken.
func TestReplacementsFollowTheStoredRingAfterTheRingPosition(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 7)
	block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
	p := int(f.st.Verifications[block].RingPosition)
	at := func(offset int) string { return ringAtRS(f, block, p+offset) }
	if set := verifiersRS(f, block); !slices.Equal(set, sortedRS(at(-2), at(-1), at(0))) {
		t.Fatalf("set %v is not the ring's positions %d-2..%d", set, p, p)
	}
	step := func(t *testing.T, out string, want string, position int) {
		t.Helper()
		before := verifiersRS(f, block)
		mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
		r := requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, before, []string{out})
		if !slices.Equal(r.Replacements, []string{want}) || int(r.RingPosition) != ((p+position)%7+7)%7 {
			t.Fatalf("replaced %s by %v at position %d, want %s at %d", out, r.Replacements, r.RingPosition, want, ((p+position)%7+7)%7)
		}
	}
	// The next node after the position.
	resyncRS(t, f, at(-1))
	step(t, at(-1), at(1), 1)
	reactivateRS(t, f, at(-1))
	// A node that is not eligible now is skipped.
	resyncRS(t, f, at(2))
	resyncRS(t, f, at(0))
	step(t, at(0), at(3), 3)
	reactivateRS(t, f, at(2))
	reactivateRS(t, f, at(0))
	// The walk continues after the new position.
	resyncRS(t, f, at(1))
	step(t, at(1), at(4), 4)
	// From position 4 the walk passes a node of the set (-2), two that earlier
	// re-selections replaced and that are Active again (-1, 0), one replaced
	// and still Syncing (1), and takes the first eligible outsider (2).
	resyncRS(t, f, at(3))
	step(t, at(3), at(2), 2)
}

// sortedRS is a sorted copy of ids.
func sortedRS(ids ...string) []string {
	out := slices.Clone(ids)
	slices.Sort(out)
	return out
}

// TestReplacedVerifiersEvidenceIsDeletedAndLateEvidenceRefused: contract
// §52.2, K75. The replaced verifiers' attestation, scan and verdict entries
// leave the record in the same Apply, the remaining verifier's evidence stays,
// late evidence of a replaced verifier is refused by the set check, and the
// replacements' evidence counts towards the quorum.
func TestReplacedVerifiersEvidenceIsDeletedAndLateEvidenceRefused(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
	block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
	set := verifiersRS(f, block)
	attestRS(t, f, block, set[0])
	passRS(t, f, block, set[1])
	kept, err := json.Marshal([]any{f.st.Verifications[block].Attestations[set[1]], f.st.Verifications[block].ByteScans[set[1]]})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	timeOutRS(t, f, block)
	mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
	r := requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, set, []string{set[0], set[2]})
	bv := f.st.Verifications[block]
	if got := slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(bv.Attestations)); !slices.Equal(got, set[1:2]) {
		t.Fatalf("attestations of %v, want %v", got, set[1:2])
	}
	if got := slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(bv.ByteScans)); !slices.Equal(got, set[1:2]) {
		t.Fatalf("scans of %v, want %v", got, set[1:2])
	}
	if got := slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(bv.Verdict.Replicas)); !slices.Equal(got, set[1:2]) || bv.Verdict.Quorum {
		t.Fatalf("verdict %+v, want only %s judged and no quorum", bv.Verdict, set[1])
	}
	if now, _ := json.Marshal([]any{bv.Attestations[set[1]], bv.ByteScans[set[1]]}); string(now) != string(kept) {
		t.Fatalf("the remaining verifier's evidence changed:\n%s\n%s", kept, now)
	}
	_, lateScan := evidenceRS(t, f, block, set[0])
	rejectStage3Unchanged(t, f, lateScan, "replica not in the block's verifier set")
	lateAttestation, _ := evidenceRS(t, f, block, set[2])
	rejectStage3Unchanged(t, f, lateAttestation, "replica not in the block's verifier set")
	passRS(t, f, block, r.Replacements[0])
	if v := f.st.Verifications[block].Verdict; !v.Quorum || v.ReselectionsAtLatch != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("verdict after a replacement's evidence = %+v, want a quorum latched at 1 re-selection", v)
	}
}

// TestReselectionIsLimitedToRingSizeMinusThree: spec §7.4. A block is
// re-selected at most ring size - 3 times; the next command is refused with
// state unchanged and the WorkSet lists the block no longer.
func TestReselectionIsLimitedToRingSizeMinusThree(t *testing.T) {
	for _, ring := range []int{4, 5} {
		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("ring of %d", ring), func(t *testing.T) {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, ring)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			for i := 0; i < ring-VerifierSelectN; i++ {
				before := verifiersRS(f, block)
				evictRS(t, f, a, before[0])
				mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
				requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, before, before[:1])
			}
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			if _, due := dueRS(t, f, block); due {
				t.Fatal("the WorkSet lists a block at its re-selection limit")
			}
			rejectStage3Unchanged(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block),
				fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d was re-selected %d times, the limit for its ring of %d", block, ring-VerifierSelectN, ring))
		})
	}
}

// TestReselectVerifiersOnAQuietTrackFiresOnTheRegistryCursor: spec §7.4,
// §17. With no further statement of the track and no other command than the
// registry cursor's advances, a verifier that never answers is replaced
// exactly when the cursor reaches evidence_timeout_l2_blocks past the
// marking, and its replacements time out from the re-selection's cursor
// block.
func TestReselectVerifiersOnAQuietTrackFiresOnTheRegistryCursor(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 7)
	block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
	set := verifiersRS(f, block)
	passRS(t, f, block, set[0])
	marked, timeout := f.st.Verifications[block].MarkedCursorBlock, f.st.Params.Stage3.EvidenceTimeoutL2Blocks
	sealed, statements := len(f.st.Blocks), f.st.NextStatementSeq
	cursorRS(t, f, marked+timeout-1)
	if row, due := dueRS(t, f, block); due {
		t.Fatalf("due before the timeout: %+v", row)
	}
	rejectStage3Unchanged(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d has no replaceable verifier", block))
	cursorRS(t, f, marked+timeout)
	row, due := dueRS(t, f, block)
	if !due || !slices.Equal(row.ExpectedSet, set) || !slices.Equal(row.Replaceable, set[1:]) {
		t.Fatalf("row at the timeout = %+v, %v; want %v replaceable", row, due, set[1:])
	}
	applied := f.ReselectionsApplied()
	mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
	r := requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, set, set[1:])
	if r.CursorBlock != marked+timeout || f.ReselectionsApplied() != applied+1 {
		t.Fatalf("cursor block %d, applied %d; want %d and %d", r.CursorBlock, f.ReselectionsApplied(), marked+timeout, applied+1)
	}
	if len(f.st.Blocks) != sealed || f.st.NextStatementSeq != statements || len(f.st.OpenBlock.StatementSeqs) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("the track was not quiet")
	}
	cursorRS(t, f, marked+2*timeout-1)
	if got := replaceableRS(f, block); got != nil {
		t.Fatalf("replaceable before the replacements time out = %v", got)
	}
	cursorRS(t, f, marked+2*timeout)
	if row, due := dueRS(t, f, block); !due || !slices.Equal(row.Replaceable, sortedRS(r.Replacements...)) {
		t.Fatalf("row at the second timeout = %+v, %v; want the replacements %v", row, due, r.Replacements)
	}
}

// TestReselectionIsRefusedAfterTheLatchAndTheVerdictSurvivesEvictionAndRestore:
// spec §7.4, §17. Two passes latch the block; the eviction of a passing
// verifier leaves the latched verdict and the set alone, a re-selection is
// refused and never listed, and a snapshot/restore round trip keeps all of
// it.
func TestReselectionIsRefusedAfterTheLatchAndTheVerdictSurvivesEvictionAndRestore(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
	block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
	set := verifiersRS(f, block)
	passRS(t, f, block, set[0])
	passRS(t, f, block, set[1])
	if v := f.st.Verifications[block].Verdict; !v.Quorum || v.ReselectionsAtLatch != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("verdict after two passes = %+v", v)
	}
	evictRS(t, f, a, set[0])
	timeOutRS(t, f, block)
	if v := f.st.Verifications[block].Verdict; !v.Quorum || !v.Replicas[set[0]].Pass || !slices.Equal(verifiersRS(f, block), set) {
		t.Fatalf("the eviction changed the latched block: %+v, set %v", v, verifiersRS(f, block))
	}
	if _, due := dueRS(t, f, block); due {
		t.Fatal("the WorkSet lists a latched block")
	}
	rejectStage3Unchanged(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block), fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d quorum has latched", block))
	record := verificationJSONOA(t, f, block)
	data := snapshotBytes(t, f)
	restoresBothWaysOA(t, f, data)
	g := restoreInto(t, data)
	if got := verificationJSONOA(t, g, block); got != record {
		t.Fatalf("restored record:\n%s\nwant\n%s", got, record)
	}
	for _, ss := range g.blockStatements(block) {
		if ss.Status != StatusQuorumVerified {
			t.Fatalf("restored statement %d is %s", ss.Seq, ss.Status)
		}
	}
}

// TestLatchRecordsTheReselectionCount: contract §52.2. The verdict that
// latches records how many re-selections the block had; a block never
// re-selected records nothing, so its verdict keeps its stage-2 bytes.
func TestLatchRecordsTheReselectionCount(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
	plain := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
	set := verifiersRS(f, plain)
	passRS(t, f, plain, set[0])
	passRS(t, f, plain, set[1])
	if v := f.st.Verifications[plain].Verdict; !v.Quorum || v.ReselectionsAtLatch != 0 || strings.Contains(verificationJSONOA(t, f, plain), "reselections") {
		t.Fatalf("a block never re-selected = %s", verificationJSONOA(t, f, plain))
	}
	block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 2)
	set = verifiersRS(f, block)
	evictRS(t, f, a, set[0])
	mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
	r := requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, set, set[:1])
	passRS(t, f, block, set[1])
	if v := f.st.Verifications[block].Verdict; v.Quorum {
		t.Fatalf("one pass latched: %+v", v)
	}
	passRS(t, f, block, r.Replacements[0])
	if v := f.st.Verifications[block].Verdict; !v.Quorum || v.ReselectionsAtLatch != 1 || !strings.Contains(verificationJSONOA(t, f, block), `"reselections_at_latch":1`) {
		t.Fatalf("latched after one re-selection = %s", verificationJSONOA(t, f, block))
	}
	restoresBothWaysOA(t, f, snapshotBytes(t, f))
}

// TestWorkSetListsReselectionDueWithTheApplyPredicate: contract §52.2. The
// ReselectionDue row lists a block exactly when Apply accepts the signed
// command over the row's expected set, names the verifiers Apply replaces,
// ascends by block and is empty while the switch is off.
func TestWorkSetListsReselectionDueWithTheApplyPredicate(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		build func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64)
		due   bool
	}{
		{"a fresh marking", func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64) {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			return f, a, markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
		}, false},
		{"an evicted verifier", func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64) {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[2])
			return f, a, block
		}, true},
		{"a verifier out of the ring", func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64) {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			resyncRS(t, f, verifiersRS(f, block)[1])
			return f, a, block
		}, true},
		{"a timeout", func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64) {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			timeOutRS(t, f, block)
			return f, a, block
		}, true},
		{"a latched quorum", func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64) {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			set := verifiersRS(f, block)
			passRS(t, f, block, set[0])
			passRS(t, f, block, set[1])
			evictRS(t, f, a, set[2])
			return f, a, block
		}, false},
		{"a challenged statement", func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64) {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			mustApply(t, f, wire.Command{OpenChallenge: &wire.OpenChallenge{BlockSeq: block, Reason: "operator review", OpenedBy: "test"}})
			return f, a, block
		}, false},
		{"the ring's limit", func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64) {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 4)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			return f, a, block
		}, false},
		{"no replacement", func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64) {
			f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 4)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			set := verifiersRS(f, block)
			evictRS(t, f, a, set[0])
			evictRS(t, f, a, set[1])
			return f, a, block
		}, false},
		{"the switch off", func(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64) {
			f, a := reselectionOffFSM(t, 6)
			block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
			evictRS(t, f, a, verifiersRS(f, block)[0])
			timeOutRS(t, f, block)
			return f, a, block
		}, false},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f, a, block := tc.build(t)
			row, due := dueRS(t, f, block)
			if due != tc.due {
				t.Fatalf("listed = %v, want %v (row %+v)", due, tc.due, row)
			}
			before := verifiersRS(f, block)
			_, applied := f.Apply(mkLog(t, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))).(Applied)
			if applied != due {
				t.Fatalf("Apply accepted = %v, the WorkSet listed = %v", applied, due)
			}
			if due {
				if !slices.Equal(row.ExpectedSet, before) {
					t.Fatalf("row expected set %v, block set %v", row.ExpectedSet, before)
				}
				requireReselectedRS(t, f, block, before, row.Replaceable)
			}
		})
	}
	t.Run("ascending by block", func(t *testing.T) {
		f, _ := reselectionFSM(t, 7)
		first := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
		second := markedBlockRS(t, f, 2)
		timeOutRS(t, f, second)
		ws, err := f.WorkSet()
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if len(ws.ReselectionDue) != 2 || ws.ReselectionDue[0].BlockSeq != first || ws.ReselectionDue[1].BlockSeq != second {
			t.Fatalf("rows = %+v, want blocks %d then %d", ws.ReselectionDue, first, second)
		}
	})
}

// forgedReselectionsRS is the container of f with block's verification
// record edited by forge.
func forgedReselectionsRS(t *testing.T, f *FSM, block uint64, forge func(bv *BlockVerification)) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	return forgedVerificationOA(t, f, block, forge)
}

// latchedReselectedRS is a block of the fixture re-selected once (its first
// verifier evicted) and then latched by the remaining verifier and the
// replacement.
func latchedReselectedRS(t *testing.T) (*FSM, uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
	block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
	set := verifiersRS(f, block)
	evictRS(t, f, a, set[0])
	mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block))
	passRS(t, f, block, set[1])
	passRS(t, f, block, lastReselectionRS(t, f, block).Replacements[0])
	if v := f.st.Verifications[block].Verdict; !v.Quorum || v.ReselectionsAtLatch != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("verdict = %+v", v)
	}
	return f, block
}

// TestRestoreRefusesAReselectionAfterTheLatch: spec §7.4, contract §52.2. A
// latched verdict must record exactly the stored number of re-selections,
// and an unlatched one none.
func TestRestoreRefusesAReselectionAfterTheLatch(t *testing.T) {
	f, block := latchedReselectedRS(t)
	restoresBothWaysOA(t, f, snapshotBytes(t, f))
	for _, recorded := range []uint32{0, 2} {
		data := forgedReselectionsRS(t, f, block, func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.Verdict.ReselectionsAtLatch = recorded })
		restoreRefusedBothWays(t, f, data, fmt.Sprintf("snapshot stage3 reselections: block %d latched with %d re-selections recorded but 1 stored", block, recorded))
	}
	g, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
	open := markedBlockRS(t, g, 1)
	evictRS(t, g, a, verifiersRS(g, open)[0])
	mustApply(t, g, reselectSetRS(t, g, a, open))
	data := forgedReselectionsRS(t, g, open, func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.Verdict.ReselectionsAtLatch = 1 })
	restoreRefusedBothWays(t, g, data, fmt.Sprintf("snapshot stage3 reselections: block %d records a re-selection count without a latched quorum", open))
}

// TestRestoreRefusesAMalformedReselection: contract §52.2. Restore checks
// every stored re-selection's structure against the stored ring, the chain
// from the marking's set to the stored set, the ring limit, the switch and
// the evidence keys, without re-deriving node status.
func TestRestoreRefusesAMalformedReselection(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 7)
	block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
	set := verifiersRS(f, block)
	passRS(t, f, block, set[0])
	timeOutRS(t, f, block)
	mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block)) // replaces set[1] and set[2]
	second := verifiersRS(f, block)
	evictRS(t, f, a, set[0])
	mustApply(t, f, reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block)) // replaces set[0]
	rs := f.st.Verifications[block].Reselections
	if len(rs) != 2 || len(rs[0].Replacements) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("fixture re-selections = %+v", rs)
	}
	restoresBothWaysOA(t, f, snapshotBytes(t, f))
	prefix := fmt.Sprintf("snapshot stage3 reselections: block %d ", block)
	outsider := slices.DeleteFunc(slices.Clone(f.st.Verifications[block].EligibleRing), func(id string) bool { return slices.Contains(second, id) })[0]
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		forge func(bv *BlockVerification)
		want  string
	}{
		{"an expected set of two", func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.Reselections[1].ExpectedSet = second[:2] },
			prefix + "re-selection 1 is malformed: expected set is not three sorted unique node ids"},
		{"a replaced id outside the expected set", func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.Reselections[1].Replaced = []string{outsider} },
			prefix + fmt.Sprintf("re-selection 1 is malformed: replaced %s is not in the expected set", outsider)},
		{"a replacement inside the expected set", func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.Reselections[1].Replacements = []string{second[0]} },
			prefix + fmt.Sprintf("re-selection 1 is malformed: replacement %s is in the expected set", second[0])},
		{"a replacement off the ring", func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.Reselections[1].Replacements = []string{"v9"} },
			prefix + fmt.Sprintf("re-selection 1 is malformed: replacements do not follow the stored ring after position %d", rs[0].RingPosition)},
		{"replacements out of ring order", func(bv *BlockVerification) { slices.Reverse(bv.Reselections[0].Replacements) },
			prefix + fmt.Sprintf("re-selection 0 is malformed: replacements do not follow the stored ring after position %d", blockSeededPosition(block, 7))},
		{"a ring position that is not the last replacement's", func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.Reselections[0].RingPosition = (rs[0].RingPosition + 1) % 7 },
			prefix + fmt.Sprintf("re-selection 0 is malformed: ring position %d is not the last replacement's %d", (rs[0].RingPosition+1)%7, rs[0].RingPosition)},
		{"a cursor block beyond the registry cursor", func(bv *BlockVerification) {
			bv.Reselections[1].CursorBlock = f.st.TableRegistry.Cursor.BlockNumber + 1
		},
			prefix + fmt.Sprintf("re-selection 1 is malformed: cursor block %d is beyond the registry cursor %d", f.st.TableRegistry.Cursor.BlockNumber+1, f.st.TableRegistry.Cursor.BlockNumber)},
		{"a cursor block below the previous one", func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.Reselections[1].CursorBlock = rs[0].CursorBlock - 1 },
			prefix + fmt.Sprintf("re-selection 1 is malformed: cursor block %d precedes the previous cursor block %d", rs[0].CursorBlock-1, rs[0].CursorBlock)},
		{"a set the records do not chain to", func(bv *BlockVerification) {
			bv.VerifierSet = sortedRS(append(slices.DeleteFunc(slices.Clone(bv.VerifierSet), func(id string) bool { return id == rs[1].Replacements[0] }), set[0])...)
		}, prefix + "re-selections do not chain to its verifier set"},
		{"a position the records do not chain to", func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.RingPosition = rs[0].RingPosition },
			prefix + "re-selections do not chain to its verifier set"},
		{"more re-selections than the ring allows", func(bv *BlockVerification) {
			bv.Reselections = append(bv.Reselections, bv.Reselections[1], bv.Reselections[1], bv.Reselections[1])
		}, prefix + "has 5 re-selections, above its ring limit 4"},
		{"evidence of a replaced verifier", func(bv *BlockVerification) {
			scan := signedScan(t, set[1], set[1][len(set[1])-1], block, nil)
			if bv.ByteScans == nil {
				bv.ByteScans = map[string]*arbiter.ByteSideScanMsg{}
			}
			bv.ByteScans[set[1]] = &scan
		},
			prefix + fmt.Sprintf("holds evidence of %s outside its verifier set", set[1])},
		{"a first expected set that is not the marking's", func(bv *BlockVerification) { bv.Reselections[0].ExpectedSet = second },
			fmt.Sprintf("block %d verifier set is not the ring's three positions ending at %d", block, blockSeededPosition(block, 7))},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			restoreRefusedBothWays(t, f, forgedReselectionsRS(t, f, block, tc.forge), tc.want)
		})
	}
	t.Run("a re-selection without the switch", func(t *testing.T) {
		g, _ := reselectionOffFSM(t, 6)
		off := markedBlockRS(t, g, 1)
		offSet := verifiersRS(g, off)
		data := forgedReselectionsRS(t, g, off, func(bv *BlockVerification) {
			bv.Reselections = []Reselection{{ExpectedSet: offSet, Replaced: offSet[:1], Replacements: outsideRS(g, off)[:1],
				RingPosition: uint32(slices.Index(bv.EligibleRing, outsideRS(g, off)[0])), CursorBlock: bv.MarkedCursorBlock, AuthorityJWS: "e30.e30.c2ln", AuthorityEpoch: g.st.ConsensusEpoch}}
		})
		restoreRefusedBothWays(t, g, data, fmt.Sprintf("snapshot stage3 reselections: block %d carries re-selections while the reselection switch is off", off))
	})
}

// TestRestoreReverifiesReselectionProofsUnderTheirEpoch: spec §7.4,
// contract §52.2. Each stored proof verifies under the authorities and
// context of the epoch it applied in, even after a rotation removed its
// signer, and a proof that does not verify under its own epoch refuses the
// container.
func TestRestoreReverifiesReselectionProofsUnderTheirEpoch(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := reselectionFSM(t, 6)
	block := markedBlockRS(t, f, 1)
	set := verifiersRS(f, block)
	evictRS(t, f, a, set[0])
	signed := reselectSetRS(t, f, a, block)
	mustApply(t, f, signed)
	epoch := f.st.ConsensusEpoch
	if r := lastReselectionRS(t, f, block); r.AuthorityEpoch != epoch || r.AuthorityJWS != signed.ReselectVerifiers.AuthorityJWS {
		t.Fatalf("stored proof %+v, want epoch %d and the command's token", r, epoch)
	}
	b, _ := authorityFixture(t)
	u := stage3Update(t, f)
	u.AuthorityAddresses = []string{b.Address()}
	mustApply(t, f, signedConsensusUpdate(t, a, u))
	if f.AuthorityAllowed(a.Address()) {
		t.Fatal("the rotation kept the old authority")
	}
	restoresBothWaysOA(t, f, snapshotBytes(t, f))
	ctx := authorityContextFor(t, f)
	ctx.AuthorityEpoch = epoch
	byB, err := b.SignReselectVerifiersWithContextAt(signed.ReselectVerifiers.Canonical(), ctx, authoritytest.Iat)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	other := signed.ReselectVerifiers.Canonical()
	other.L3BlockSeq = block + 1
	otherBlock, err := a.SignReselectVerifiersWithContextAt(other, ctx, authoritytest.Iat)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	prefix := fmt.Sprintf("snapshot block %d re-selection 0 proof: ", block)
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		forge func(r *Reselection)
		want  string
	}{
		{"the next epoch", func(r *Reselection) { r.AuthorityEpoch = epoch + 1 }, prefix},
		{"a key that was no authority then", func(r *Reselection) { r.AuthorityJWS = byB }, prefix},
		{"a token of another block", func(r *Reselection) { r.AuthorityJWS = otherBlock }, prefix},
		{"an epoch beyond the history", func(r *Reselection) { r.AuthorityEpoch = epoch + 5 },
			prefix + fmt.Sprintf("authority epoch %d is beyond the consensus epoch %d", epoch+5, epoch+1)},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			data := forgedReselectionsRS(t, f, block, func(bv *BlockVerification) { tc.forge(&bv.Reselections[0]) })
			restoreRefusedBothWays(t, f, data, tc.want)
		})
	}
}

// TestSnapshotBelowV21RefusesReselectionFields: plan S3-E2 contract §46. A
// stored re-selection or a latch count is stage-3 state, refused in a
// container below v21.
func TestSnapshotBelowV21RefusesReselectionFields(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := tracksFSM(t)
	data := snapshotBytes(t, f)
	if data[4] >= snapshotVersionV21 {
		t.Fatalf("the tracks fixture writes v%d", data[4])
	}
	for name, field := range map[string]func(bv map[string]any){
		"reselections": func(bv map[string]any) {
			bv["reselections"] = []any{map[string]any{"expected_set": []any{"v1", "v2", "v3"}, "replaced": []any{"v1"}, "replacements": []any{"v4"},
				"ring_position": 3, "cursor_block": 151, "authority_jws": "e30.e30.c2ln", "authority_epoch": 1}}
		},
		"reselections_at_latch": func(bv map[string]any) {
			bv["verdict"].(map[string]any)["reselections_at_latch"] = 1
		},
	} {

			forged := rewriteSnapshotDocument(t, data, data[4], func(doc map[string]any) {
				field(doc["verifications"].(map[string]any)["1"].(map[string]any))
			})
			if err := restoreErr(t, forged); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "stage3 state is present in a pre-v21 container") {
				t.Fatalf("restore = %v", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestBlockVerificationViewCopiesTheReselections: contract §52.2. The view
// carries the stored re-selections whole, detached from state, and the
// latch count.
func TestBlockVerificationViewCopiesTheReselections(t *testing.T) {

		t.Fatal("the view aliases the stored re-selection")

Create `fsm/reselect_verifiers.go`:

```go
package fsm

import (
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"slices"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// ReselectVerifiers, stage-3 switch 7 (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §7.4,
// §10.4 step 7; plan S3-E3 contract §52.2, clarification K75). The leader
// replaces the verifiers of a marked, unlatched, unchallenged block that lack
// complete evidence and are evicted, no longer eligible or timed out on the
// committed L2 registry cursor, and an evicted verifier whatever its
// evidence, with the next nodes of the ring stored at the marking. The
// replaced verifiers' evidence is deleted in the same Apply, so their late
// evidence is refused by the verifier-set check of applyRecordAttestation and
// applyRecordByteSideScan, and restore requires every evidence key to name a
// member of the set. Each applied command appends a Reselection with its
// signed expected set, the registry cursor block and its authority proof; the
// verdict that latches records how many the block had, so no re-selection
// can follow the latch. Nothing here runs before the reselection switch.

// applyReselectVerifiers applies Raft tag 39. The refusals run in the order
// of contract §52.2, and every one leaves state unchanged.
func (f *FSM) applyReselectVerifiers(c *wire.ReselectVerifiers) any {
	if !f.reselectionOnLocked() {
		return Rejected{Reason: "re-selection is refused until the reselection switch is on"}
	}
	if len(c.ExpectedSet) != VerifierSelectN || !ringIsSortedAndUnique(c.ExpectedSet) {
		return Rejected{Reason: "reselect verifiers: expected_set must be 3 sorted unique node ids"}
	}
	bv := f.st.Verifications[c.L3BlockSeq]
	if c.L3BlockSeq == 0 || c.L3BlockSeq > uint64(len(f.st.Blocks)) || bv == nil {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: unknown block %d", c.L3BlockSeq)}
	}
	if len(bv.VerifierSet) == 0 {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d is not marked replaying", c.L3BlockSeq)}
	}
	kind := fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers block %d", c.L3BlockSeq)
	if reason := f.authorityCommandRefusalLocked(kind, func(v *authority.Validator, ctx authority.ConsensusContext) error {
		_, err := v.VerifyReselectVerifiers(c.Canonical(), c.AuthorityJWS, ctx)
		return err
	}); reason != "" {
		return Rejected{Reason: reason}
	}
	if !slices.Equal(c.ExpectedSet, bv.VerifierSet) {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: expected_set differs from the verifier set of block %d", c.L3BlockSeq)}
	}
	replaced, replacements, position, reason := f.reselectionPlanLocked(c.L3BlockSeq, bv)
	if reason != "" {
		return Rejected{Reason: reason}
	}
	cursor := f.registryCursorBlockLocked()
	// Every check has passed; mutate. The replaced verifiers' evidence leaves
	// the record (K75), the set takes the replacements, and the stored ring
	// position moves to the last replacement.
	for _, id := range replaced {
		delete(bv.Attestations, id)
		delete(bv.ByteScans, id)
		if bv.Verdict != nil {
			delete(bv.Verdict.Replicas, id)
		}
	}
	set := slices.DeleteFunc(slices.Clone(bv.VerifierSet), func(id string) bool { return slices.Contains(replaced, id) })
	set = append(set, replacements...)
	slices.Sort(set)
	bv.VerifierSet, bv.RingPosition = set, position
	bv.Reselections = append(bv.Reselections, Reselection{
		ExpectedSet:    slices.Clone(c.ExpectedSet),
		Replaced:       replaced,
		Replacements:   replacements,
		RingPosition:   position,
		CursorBlock:    cursor,
		AuthorityJWS:   c.AuthorityJWS,
		AuthorityEpoch: f.st.ConsensusEpoch,
	})
	f.reselectionsApplied++
	f.emit(Event{Kind: EventEvidenceRecorded, BlockSeq: c.L3BlockSeq})
	f.reevaluateBlock(c.L3BlockSeq)
	return Applied{}
}

// registryCursorBlockLocked is the committed table-registry cursor's L2
// block, 0 before the registry exists.
func (f *FSM) registryCursorBlockLocked() uint64 {
	if reg := f.st.TableRegistry; reg != nil {
		return reg.Cursor.BlockNumber
	}
	return 0
}

// reselectionPlanLocked is the half of ReselectVerifiers that reads only the
// block and committed state: refusals 7 to 11 of contract §52.2, in that
// order, or the sorted replaceable verifiers, their replacements in ring
// order and the last ring position used. Apply and the WorkSet's
// ReselectionDue row share it, so the leader proposes exactly what Apply
// accepts.
func (f *FSM) reselectionPlanLocked(blockSeq uint64, bv *BlockVerification) (replaced, replacements []string, position uint32, reason string) {
	switch {
	case bv.Verdict != nil && bv.Verdict.Quorum:
		return nil, nil, 0, fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d quorum has latched", blockSeq)
	case blockChallenged(f.blockStatements(blockSeq)):
		return nil, nil, 0, fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d has a challenged statement", blockSeq)
	case len(bv.Reselections)+VerifierSelectN >= len(bv.EligibleRing):
		// A block marked before owner_aware_selection stores no ring, so its
		// limit is 0 and it is never re-selected.
		return nil, nil, 0, fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d was re-selected %d times, the limit for its ring of %d",
			blockSeq, len(bv.Reselections), len(bv.EligibleRing))
	}
	replaced = f.replaceableVerifiersLocked(blockSeq, bv)
	if len(replaced) == 0 {
		return nil, nil, 0, fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d has no replaceable verifier", blockSeq)
	}
	owner, _ := f.blockTrackLocked(blockSeq) // replaceableVerifiersLocked found the track
	replacements, position, reason = f.reselectionReplacementsLocked(bv, replaced, owner)
	if reason != "" {
		return nil, nil, 0, reason
	}
	return replaced, replacements, position, ""
}

// replaceableVerifiersLocked lists, sorted, the verifiers of bv's set that a
// re-selection may replace now (spec §7.4): one without complete evidence
// that is evicted, no longer in the block's eligible ring, or timed out on
// the committed registry cursor, and one with complete evidence only when it
// is evicted. A block without a track was sealed before the tracks
// activation and has none.
func (f *FSM) replaceableVerifiersLocked(blockSeq uint64, bv *BlockVerification) []string {
	owner, ok := f.blockTrackLocked(blockSeq)
	if !ok {
		return nil
	}
	eligible := f.eligibleRingLocked(owner, bv.SourceNodes, bv.groupSeal())
	timedOut := f.reselectionTimedOutLocked(bv)
	var out []string
	for _, id := range bv.VerifierSet {
		complete := bv.Attestations[id] != nil && bv.ByteScans[id] != nil
		if f.evictedNodeLocked(id) || (!complete && (timedOut || !slices.Contains(eligible, id))) {
			out = append(out, id)
		}
	}
	slices.Sort(out)
	return out
}

// reselectionTimedOutLocked reports that the committed registry cursor has
// advanced at least evidence_timeout_l2_blocks past the larger of the
// block's marking and its last re-selection (K75). The table-registry
// watcher advances the cursor every cursor_advance_interval whatever the
// track's traffic, so the timeout fires on a quiet track too.
func (f *FSM) reselectionTimedOutLocked(bv *BlockVerification) bool {
	params := f.st.Params.Stage3
	if params == nil || f.st.TableRegistry == nil {
		return false
	}
	since := bv.MarkedCursorBlock
	if n := len(bv.Reselections); n > 0 {
		since = max(since, bv.Reselections[n-1].CursorBlock)
	}
	cursor := f.registryCursorBlockLocked()
	return cursor >= since && cursor-since >= params.EvidenceTimeoutL2Blocks
}

// reselectionReplacementsLocked walks the stored ring from
// bv.RingPosition+1 cyclically, at most once around, taking one node per
// replaced verifier in sorted order and skipping a node that is in the
// current set, that an earlier re-selection of the block replaced, or that
// is not in the block's eligible ring now (spec §7.4). position is the ring
// index of the last node taken.
func (f *FSM) reselectionReplacementsLocked(bv *BlockVerification, replaced []string, owner uint64) (replacements []string, position uint32, reason string) {
	ring := bv.EligibleRing
	eligible := f.eligibleRingLocked(owner, bv.SourceNodes, bv.groupSeal())
	step := 0
	for _, id := range replaced {
		found := false
		for step < len(ring) {
			step++
			index := (int(bv.RingPosition) + step) % len(ring)
			candidate := ring[index]
			if slices.Contains(bv.VerifierSet, candidate) || reselectionReplaced(bv.Reselections, candidate) || !slices.Contains(eligible, candidate) {
				continue
			}
			replacements = append(replacements, candidate)
			position = uint32(index)
			found = true
			break
		}
		if !found {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Sprintf("reselect verifiers: block %d has no replacement for %s", bv.BlockSeq, id)
		}
	}
	return replacements, position, ""
}

// reselectionReplaced reports that a stored re-selection of the block
// replaced id.
func reselectionReplaced(reselections []Reselection, id string) bool {
	for _, r := range reselections {
		if slices.Contains(r.Replaced, id) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// reselectionDueLocked is the WorkSet.ReselectionDue row of a marked block:
// present exactly when reselectionPlanLocked accepts it now.
func (f *FSM) reselectionDueLocked(blockSeq uint64, bv *BlockVerification) (ReselectionWork, bool) {
	replaced, _, _, reason := f.reselectionPlanLocked(blockSeq, bv)
	if reason != "" {
		return ReselectionWork{}, false
	}
	return ReselectionWork{BlockSeq: blockSeq, ExpectedSet: cloneStrings(bv.VerifierSet), Replaceable: replaced}, true
}

// ReselectionsApplied is the number of ReselectVerifiers commands this
// replica's FSM applied since process start
// (arbiter_verifier_reselections_total). It is node-local: never
// snapshotted, and a Restore does not reset it.
func (f *FSM) ReselectionsApplied() uint64 {
	f.mu.RLock()
	defer f.mu.RUnlock()
	return f.reselectionsApplied
}

// cloneReselections is a detached copy of a block's stored re-selections.
func cloneReselections(in []Reselection) []Reselection {
	if in == nil {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]Reselection, len(in))
	for i, r := range in {
		r.ExpectedSet = slices.Clone(r.ExpectedSet)
		r.Replaced = slices.Clone(r.Replaced)
		r.Replacements = slices.Clone(r.Replacements)
		out[i] = r
	}
	return out
}

// verificationHasReselectionFields reports a verification record carrying a
// stored re-selection or a latch count; stage3FieldsPresent refuses either
// under a pre-v21 version byte.
func verificationHasReselectionFields(bv *BlockVerification) bool {
	return bv != nil && (len(bv.Reselections) > 0 || (bv.Verdict != nil && bv.Verdict.ReselectionsAtLatch != 0))
}

// validateStage3Reselections checks every stored re-selection structurally
// (spec §7.4, contract §52.2): a block carries re-selections only with the
// reselection switch and at most ring size - 3 of them; each has an expected
// set of three sorted unique ids, replaced ids from that set and
// replacements outside it that no earlier re-selection replaced, taken from
// the stored ring in walk order after the previous position, a ring position
// at its last replacement and a cursor block between the previous one and
// the committed cursor; the records chain from the marking's set to the
// stored set and position; a latched verdict records exactly the stored
// count and an unlatched one none; and no evidence of a block marked from a
// ring names a node outside its set. validateStage3Selection has already
// required the first expected set to be the ring's three positions at the
// block-seeded position. Node status is never re-derived.
func validateStage3Reselections(st *State) error {
	on := stage3SwitchValue(st.Params.Stage3, Stage3SwitchReselection)
	var cursor uint64
	if st.TableRegistry != nil {
		cursor = st.TableRegistry.Cursor.BlockNumber
	}
	for seq := uint64(1); seq <= uint64(len(st.Blocks)); seq++ {
		bv := st.Verifications[seq]
		if bv == nil {
			continue // validateLatchedConsensus refuses a block without its record
		}
		if err := validateBlockReselections(seq, bv, on, cursor); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("snapshot stage3 reselections: %w", err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// validateBlockReselections is validateStage3Reselections for one block.
func validateBlockReselections(seq uint64, bv *BlockVerification, on bool, cursor uint64) error {
	n := len(bv.Reselections)
	if n > 0 {
		if !on {
			return fmt.Errorf("block %d carries re-selections while the reselection switch is off", seq)
		}
		if limit := max(len(bv.EligibleRing)-VerifierSelectN, 0); n > limit {
			return fmt.Errorf("block %d has %d re-selections, above its ring limit %d", seq, n, limit)
		}
		ring := bv.EligibleRing
		position := blockSeededPosition(seq, len(ring))
		since := bv.MarkedCursorBlock
		var replaced []string
		for i, r := range bv.Reselections {
			if reason := reselectionMalformed(r, ring, position, since, cursor, replaced); reason != "" {
				return fmt.Errorf("block %d re-selection %d is malformed: %s", seq, i, reason)
			}
			replaced = append(replaced, r.Replaced...)
			position, since = r.RingPosition, r.CursorBlock
		}
		for i, r := range bv.Reselections {
			next := slices.DeleteFunc(slices.Clone(r.ExpectedSet), func(id string) bool { return slices.Contains(r.Replaced, id) })
			next = append(next, r.Replacements...)
			slices.Sort(next)
			want := bv.VerifierSet
			if i+1 < n {
				want = bv.Reselections[i+1].ExpectedSet
			}
			if !slices.Equal(next, want) {
				return fmt.Errorf("block %d re-selections do not chain to its verifier set", seq)
			}
		}
		if bv.RingPosition != position {
			return fmt.Errorf("block %d re-selections do not chain to its verifier set", seq)
		}
	}
	if v := bv.Verdict; v != nil {
		switch {
		case v.Quorum && int(v.ReselectionsAtLatch) != n:
			return fmt.Errorf("block %d latched with %d re-selections recorded but %d stored", seq, v.ReselectionsAtLatch, n)
		case !v.Quorum && v.ReselectionsAtLatch != 0:
			return fmt.Errorf("block %d records a re-selection count without a latched quorum", seq)
		}
	}
	if n > 0 || len(bv.EligibleRing) > 0 {
		evidence := slices.Concat(slices.Collect(maps.Keys(bv.Attestations)), slices.Collect(maps.Keys(bv.ByteScans)))
		if bv.Verdict != nil {
			evidence = append(evidence, slices.Collect(maps.Keys(bv.Verdict.Replicas))...)
		}
		slices.Sort(evidence)
		for _, id := range evidence {
			if !slices.Contains(bv.VerifierSet, id) {
				return fmt.Errorf("block %d holds evidence of %s outside its verifier set", seq, id)
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// reselectionMalformed is the first structural fault of one stored
// re-selection, given the ring position and cursor block before it and the
// ids earlier re-selections of the block replaced, or "".
func reselectionMalformed(r Reselection, ring []string, previous uint32, since, cursor uint64, replaced []string) string {
	if len(r.ExpectedSet) != VerifierSelectN || !ringIsSortedAndUnique(r.ExpectedSet) {
		return "expected set is not three sorted unique node ids"
	}
	if len(r.Replaced) == 0 || !ringIsSortedAndUnique(r.Replaced) {
		return "replaced is empty, unsorted or repeated"
	}
	for _, id := range r.Replaced {
		if !slices.Contains(r.ExpectedSet, id) {
			return fmt.Sprintf("replaced %s is not in the expected set", id)
		}
	}
	if len(r.Replacements) != len(r.Replaced) {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d replacements for %d replaced", len(r.Replacements), len(r.Replaced))
	}
	walked := -1
	for _, id := range r.Replacements {
		if slices.Contains(r.ExpectedSet, id) {
			return fmt.Sprintf("replacement %s is in the expected set", id)
		}
		if slices.Contains(replaced, id) {
			return fmt.Sprintf("replacement %s was replaced by an earlier re-selection", id)
		}
		index := slices.Index(ring, id)
		if index < 0 {
			return fmt.Sprintf("replacements do not follow the stored ring after position %d", previous)
		}
		offset := (index - int(previous) - 1 + 2*len(ring)) % len(ring)
		if offset <= walked {
			return fmt.Sprintf("replacements do not follow the stored ring after position %d", previous)
		}
		walked = offset
	}
	if last := uint32(slices.Index(ring, r.Replacements[len(r.Replacements)-1])); r.RingPosition != last {
		return fmt.Sprintf("ring position %d is not the last replacement's %d", r.RingPosition, last)
	}
	if r.CursorBlock < since {
		return fmt.Sprintf("cursor block %d precedes the previous cursor block %d", r.CursorBlock, since)
	}
	if r.CursorBlock > cursor {
		return fmt.Sprintf("cursor block %d is beyond the registry cursor %d", r.CursorBlock, cursor)
	}
	return ""
}

// validateReselectionProofs re-verifies every stored re-selection's
// authority proof under the authorities and context of the epoch it applied
// in (spec §7.4), the way validateConsensusHistory re-verifies promotion and
// cleanup proofs; node status is not re-derived. Blocks are visited in
// order, so every replica names the same corruption.
func validateReselectionProofs(st *State, paramsByEpoch []Params, genesisID string) error {
	for seq := uint64(1); seq <= uint64(len(st.Blocks)); seq++ {
		bv := st.Verifications[seq]
		if bv == nil {
			continue
		}
		for i, r := range bv.Reselections {
			if err := reselectionProofError(seq, r, paramsByEpoch, genesisID); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("snapshot block %d re-selection %d proof: %w", seq, i, err)
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// reselectionProofError verifies one stored proof under paramsByEpoch of its
// own epoch.
func reselectionProofError(seq uint64, r Reselection, paramsByEpoch []Params, genesisID string) error {
	if r.AuthorityEpoch >= uint64(len(paramsByEpoch)) {
		return fmt.Errorf("authority epoch %d is beyond the consensus epoch %d", r.AuthorityEpoch, len(paramsByEpoch)-1)
	}
	params := paramsByEpoch[r.AuthorityEpoch]
	validator := authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: authorityAddressSet(params.AuthorityAddresses)}
	ctx := authority.ConsensusContext{NetworkID: params.NetworkID, GenesisSnapshotID: genesisID, AuthorityEpoch: r.AuthorityEpoch}
	_, err := validator.VerifyReselectVerifiers(arbiter.ReselectVerifiersCommand{L3BlockSeq: seq, ExpectedSet: r.ExpectedSet}, r.AuthorityJWS, ctx)
	return err
}
```

// TestGetBlockVerificationServesReselections: plan S3-E3 contract §52.2.
// GetBlockVerification serves every stored re-selection in order, its
// replacements in the stored ring order and without its signed expected set
// (D33), and the latch count, detached from the view; a block never
// re-selected serves neither.
func TestGetBlockVerificationServesReselections(t *testing.T) {
	view := stage3BlockVerificationView()
	view.Reselections = []fsm.Reselection{
		{ExpectedSet: []string{"v1", "v2", "v3"}, Replaced: []string{"v2", "v3"}, Replacements: []string{"v5", "v4"}, RingPosition: 3,
			CursorBlock: 190, AuthorityJWS: "h.p.s1", AuthorityEpoch: 4},
		{ExpectedSet: []string{"v1", "v4", "v5"}, Replaced: []string{"v1"}, Replacements: []string{"v6"}, RingPosition: 5,
			CursorBlock: 220, AuthorityJWS: "h.p.s2", AuthorityEpoch: 5},
	}
	view.ReselectionsAtLatch = 2
	got := blockVerificationToPB(view)
	want := []*pb.BlockReselection{
		{Replaced: []string{"v2", "v3"}, Replacements: []string{"v5", "v4"}, RingPosition: 3, CursorBlock: 190, AuthorityJws: "h.p.s1", AuthorityEpoch: 4},
		{Replaced: []string{"v1"}, Replacements: []string{"v6"}, RingPosition: 5, CursorBlock: 220, AuthorityJws: "h.p.s2", AuthorityEpoch: 5},
	}
	if len(got.GetReselections()) != len(want) || got.GetReselectionsAtLatch() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("served %v at latch %d, want %v at 2", got.GetReselections(), got.GetReselectionsAtLatch(), want)
	}
	for i := range want {
		if !proto.Equal(got.GetReselections()[i], want[i]) {
			t.Fatalf("re-selection %d = %v, want %v", i, got.GetReselections()[i], want[i])
		}
	}
	if fields := (&pb.BlockReselection{}).ProtoReflect().Descriptor().Fields(); fields.Len() != 6 || fields.ByName("expected_set") != nil {
		t.Fatalf("BlockReselection has %d fields; the signed expected set must stay unserved", fields.Len())
	}
	view.Reselections[0].Replaced[0], view.Reselections[0].Replacements[0] = "mutated", "mutated"
	if r := got.GetReselections()[0]; r.GetReplaced()[0] != "v2" || r.GetReplacements()[0] != "v5" {
		t.Fatalf("the served re-selection aliases the view: %v", r)
	}
	plain := stage3BlockVerificationView()
	plain.Reselections, plain.ReselectionsAtLatch = nil, 0
	if p := blockVerificationToPB(plain); p.GetReselections() != nil || p.GetReselectionsAtLatch() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("a block never re-selected serves %v at latch %d", p.GetReselections(), p.GetReselectionsAtLatch())
	}
}

// captureReselectionsO records every ReselectVerifiers node is asked to apply
// and answers it with a rejection, so the FSM never changes; every other

func captureReselectionsO(node *fakeNode) *[]wire.ReselectVerifiers {

	}
	return &got

// local authority signer in the current consensus context; a refusal is not

func TestOrchestratorProposesASignedReselection(t *testing.T) {

	got := captureReselectionsO(node)
	ws := fsm.WorkSet{ReselectionDue: []fsm.ReselectionWork{
		{BlockSeq: 4, ExpectedSet: []string{"v1", "v2", "v3"}, Replaceable: []string{"v2"}},
		{BlockSeq: 7, ExpectedSet: []string{"v2", "v4", "v5"}, Replaceable: []string{"v4", "v5"}},
	}}
	if err := o.handleWorkSet(t.Context(), ws); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("handleWorkSet: %v", err)
	}
	if len(*got) != len(ws.ReselectionDue) {
		t.Fatalf("proposed %d re-selections, want %d", len(*got), len(ws.ReselectionDue))
	}
	view, err := f.ConsensusParamsView()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ctx := authority.ConsensusContext{NetworkID: view.Current.NetworkID, GenesisSnapshotID: view.GenesisSnapshotID, AuthorityEpoch: view.Epoch}
	validator := &authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: map[string]bool{strings.ToLower(signer.Address()): true}}
	for i, row := range ws.ReselectionDue {
		c := (*got)[i]
		if c.L3BlockSeq != row.BlockSeq || !slices.Equal(c.ExpectedSet, row.ExpectedSet) {
			t.Fatalf("proposal %d = block %d over %v, want block %d over %v", i, c.L3BlockSeq, c.ExpectedSet, row.BlockSeq, row.ExpectedSet)
		}
		if _, err := validator.VerifyReselectVerifiers(c.Canonical(), c.AuthorityJWS, ctx); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("proposal %d does not verify under the leader's context: %v", i, err)
		}
	}
	_, unsignedNode, _, _, _, unsigned, _ := newHarness(t, params)
	seedGenesisWriterAndVerifiers(t, unsignedNode)
	none := captureReselectionsO(unsignedNode)
	if err := unsigned.handleWorkSet(t.Context(), ws); err != nil || len(*none) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("without a signer: %v, %d proposals", err, len(*none))
	}
}

	params, signer := authorityParamsO(t)

	}
	for pass := 1; pass <= 3; pass++ {
		if err := o.handleWorkSet(t.Context(), ws); err != nil {

		}
	}
	if len(*got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("proposed %d re-selections before the switch", len(*got))
	}
}

- [ ] **Step 20: Propose the due re-selections**

Create `orchestrator/reselect.go`:

```go
package orchestrator

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"slices"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter/fsm"
)

// handleReselections proposes, for every WorkSet.ReselectionDue row in
// order, the ReselectVerifiers of the row's block over its expected set,
// signed by the local authority signer in the current consensus context
// (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §7.4; plan S3-E3 contract §52.2). The FSM lists
// a row only while the reselection switch is on and Apply would accept the
// command, so nothing is proposed before the switch. A refusal (ErrRejected)
// means the block changed after the WorkSet read; the next pass re-reads
// it, as for MarkReplaying. There is no operator RPC for re-selection
// (clarification K75).
func (o *Loop) handleReselections(ctx context.Context, ws fsm.WorkSet) error {
	for _, row := range ws.ReselectionDue {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if !o.authoritySignerReady("verifier reselection") {
			return nil
		}
		signingContext, ready := o.authoritySigningContext("verifier reselection signing")
		if !ready {
			return nil
		}
		cmd := wire.ReselectVerifiers{L3BlockSeq: row.BlockSeq, ExpectedSet: slices.Clone(row.ExpectedSet)}
		jws, err := o.d.Signer.SignReselectVerifiersWithContext(cmd.Canonical(), signingContext)
		if err != nil {
			o.d.Logger.Warn("sign reselect verifiers failed", "block", row.BlockSeq, "err", err)
			continue
		}
		cmd.AuthorityJWS = jws
		o.d.Logger.Info("verifier reselection", "block", row.BlockSeq, "expected_set", row.ExpectedSet, "replaceable", row.Replaceable)
		if _, err := o.propose(ctx, wire.Command{ReselectVerifiers: &cmd}); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, ErrRejected) {
			return fmt.Errorf("reselect verifiers block %d: %w", row.BlockSeq, err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

## Task 75: arbiter — MemberCheckpoint, member classes and MarkMemberLagging (S3-E3)

Spec §9.1, §9.2 and §10.4 step 8 make `checkpoints` the eighth stage-3 switch: from it a replicate member states, with its verifiers-entry `replica_signer`, that its copies of the listed groups' tables equal a published manifest at its owner's entry, and every member's class in a group follows from that entry. This task adds the FSM, transport, leader and operator halves (contract §52.3, clarifications K76 and K77):
- `MemberCheckpoint` (Raft tag 41) with the fourteen refusals of §52.3, a `checkpoint_seq` stored per (member, owner) with the `replica_signer` that accepted it, published in the registry view, kept through group removal, leaving and re-registration, and restarted only when the signer rotates;
- the classes `bootstrapping`, `caught_up`, `behind` and `lagging` with the lag_low hysteresis, over each owner's bounded `OwnerAdvances` ring of its last `max_lag_publications + 1` published advances, which every publication appends to while the switch is on, a quarantined owner excepted, and which a lowered `max_lag_publications` trims at once;
- `MarkMemberLagging` (Raft tag 42), its leader-local timeout proposal (`dispatch.member_lagging_timeout`, default `30m`, `0` disables) through the new `WorkSet.MemberLag` row, `ConsensusAdmin.MarkMemberLagging` and `arbiter-admin member lagging`;
- `VerifierGateway.SubmitMemberCheckpoint`;
- the served `checkpoint`, `observed_entry`, saturating `lag_advances` (D31) and `member_checkpoint_seqs`, with the registry-version bump of a publication that can change a served lag (§50);
- the restore rule `validateStage3Checkpoints`, which also binds every stored checkpoint, a Leaving record's included, to a published manifest whose `track_frontiers` entry for its owner is its entry (refusals 12 and 13 again) and every recent advance to an entry a published manifest carries for its owner, the per-epoch `replica_signer` re-verification `validateMemberCheckpointProofs`, and the interned-body round trip of the whole group layer (`TestInternedBodyKeepsTheGroupLayer`).

With the switch off nothing of it runs: both Apply arms refuse first with the K67 texts, the WorkSet row is nil, `recordOwnerAdvanceLocked` is never called, and every new field is `omitempty`, so each Apply, snapshot and chain hash stays byte for byte Task 74's.
